<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 1+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Feather Token](/Equipment.aspx?ID=244)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 570

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Each feather token appears to be a simple feather from some exotic bird. The feather’s shaft, dipped in gold, bears a single arcane rune. Activating a feather token causes it to transform into another object, which then can be used as normal for that object. Each feather can be activated only once, with most of them permanently becoming the item in their description.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
level="2"
right="Item 7"
pfs="Standard"
>
Feather Token (Anchor)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 570

**Price** 55 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

This feather can be activated only on a boat. When activated, this feather transforms into a massive anchor that causes the boat to immediately stop. After 1 day, the anchor vanishes and the boat can move as normal. The anchor is attached to the boat by a magical chain of force, but the chain can be removed by [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) or destroyed (Hardness 30, HP 40).

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Feather Token (Bird)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 570

**Price** 8 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

When activated, this token transforms into a small sparrow that waits on your finger for you to relay a message up to 1 minute in length, along with the name and rough location of a recipient. The recipient must be someone you have met, and the location must be somewhere you have visited. After receiving the message, the bird flies off to deliver it, traveling at 30 miles per hour and then searching for the target in the location you provided. If the bird finds the target, it moves adjacent to them, your words emanate from the bird, and the bird then flies off and vanishes. The bird also vanishes if it fails to find your target after 10 hours of searching the location you specified.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Feather Token (Chest)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 570

**Price** 10 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

When you use this token, a small wooden chest appears and immediately opens. This chest can hold up to 10 Bulk worth of items. Once the chest is closed, it transforms again—this time into a key—taking all of the stored items with it. You can activate this key by spending an Interact action to turn it in an imaginary lock, which causes it to transform back into a chest with all of the items still inside. Once it has turned into a chest a second time, it forever remains a wooden chest.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 4"
pfs="Standard"
>
Feather Token (Fan)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 570

**Price** 15 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

Activating this feather requires you to fan it in a given direction. If this direction is toward the sail of a vessel, the feather flutters up toward the sail and fans continuously, filling the sail with air and granting the vessel a +10-foot circumstance bonus to its Speed for 8 hours. If fanned in any other direction, it instead produces a single casting of [_gust of wind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=143) (DC 20).

<title
level="2"
right="Item 2"
pfs="Standard"
>
Feather Token (Holly Bush)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 570

**Price** 6 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

When this feather is activated, it immediately transforms into a living holly bush, filling a single square. This bush can provide standard cover. In addition, the bush has 2d4 bright-red berries. While holly berries are usually poisonous, these berries are infused with beneficial magic. You can pick and eat a berry as an Interact action to recover 1 Hit Point. Once plucked from the bush, a berry becomes non-magical after a few seconds, so it doesn’t heal you if you don’t eat it within the span of your Interact action.

 If activated on soil, the plant continues to grow and thrive (although it doesn’t produce any more healing berries). If activated elsewhere, it withers and dies within 1d4 days.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 1"
pfs="Standard"
>
Feather Token (Ladder)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 570

**Price** 3 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

When activated, this feather transforms permanently into a 20-foot-long wooden ladder.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 8"
pfs="Standard"
>
Feather Token (Swan Boat)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 570

**Price** 76 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

This feather can be activated only when tossed into a large body of water, such as a lake or broad river. It transforms into a swan-shaped boat capable of carrying up to 32 Medium creatures, 8 Large creatures, or 2 Huge creatures. The boat moves on the water at a Speed of 50 feet, and lasts 1 day.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 6"
pfs="Standard"
>
Feather Token (Tree)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 570

**Price** 38 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

This token can be activated only on an unoccupied patch of earth or soil. When activated, this token transforms into an oak tree, 60 feet tall with a 5-foot-wide trunk. The tree continues to live and grow if conditions are favorable.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 9"
pfs="Standard"
>
Feather Token (Whip)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 570

**Price** 130 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

This feather transforms into a _+1 striking [dancing whip_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=293) when activated. The whip immediately jumps from your grasp and proceeds to attack your enemies until 1 minute has passed or it fails its flat check for _dancing_, at which point it vanishes. If the whip’s target isn’t prone, the whip uses its actions to attempt to Trip that creature instead of making a Strike. The whip’s total attack modifier for Striking or Tripping is +18 instead of the normal bonus for a _dancing_ weapon.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 6"
pfs="Limited"
>
Feather Token (Balloon)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder Special: Fumbus](/Sources.aspx?ID=105)

**Price** 50 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

This feather can't be activated underwater. When activated, the feather transforms into a balloon of waxed cloth that is 3 feet in diameter and filled with hot air. Handles on the bottom of the balloon allow up to two creatures sized Medium or smaller to hold onto the balloon. One round after being activated, the balloon rises up into the air at a speed of 20 feet per round. After rising for 3 rounds, the balloon floats in place for two rounds as the air inside cools, then descends at a speed of 20 feet per round. When the balloon reaches its original elevation, the balloon deflates.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Limited"
>
Feather Token (Puddle)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder Special: Fumbus](/Sources.aspx?ID=105)

**Price** 8 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

When activated, the feather transforms into two gallons of fresh, clear water. If no one drinks it, the water evaporates after 1 day.

Item 3 Feather Token (Bird) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 8 gp When activated, this token transforms into a small sparrow that waits on your finger for you to relay a message up to 1 minute in length, along with the name and rough location of a recipient. The recipient must be someone you have met, and the location must be somewhere you have visited. After receiving the message, the bird flies off to deliver it, traveling at 30 miles per hour and then searching for the target in the location you provided. If the bird finds the target, it moves adjacent to them, your words emanate from the bird, and the bird then flies off and vanishes. The bird also vanishes if it fails to find your target after 10 hours of searching the location you specified. Item 3 Feather Token (Chest) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 10 gp When you use this token, a small wooden chest appears and immediately opens. This chest can hold up to 10 Bulk worth of items. Once the chest is closed, it transforms again—this time into a key—taking all of the stored items with it. You can activate this key by spending an Interact action to turn it in an imaginary lock, which causes it to transform back into a chest with all of the items still inside. Once it has turned into a chest a second time, it forever remains a wooden chest. Item 4 Feather Token (Fan) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 15 gp Activating this feather requires you to fan it in a given direction. If this direction is toward the sail of a vessel, the feather flutters up toward the sail and fans continuously, filling the sail with air and granting the vessel a +10-foot circumstance bonus to its Speed for 8 hours. If fanned in any other direction, it instead produces a single casting of gust of wind (DC 20). Item 2 Feather Token (Holly Bush) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 6 gp When this feather is activated, it immediately transforms into a living holly bush, filling a single square. This bush can provide standard cover. In addition, the bush has 2d4 bright-red berries. While holly berries are usually poisonous, these berries are infused with beneficial magic. You can pick and eat a berry as an Interact action to recover 1 Hit Point. Once plucked from the bush, a berry becomes non-magical after a few seconds, so it doesn’t heal you if you don’t eat it within the span of your Interact action. If activated on soil, the plant continues to grow and thrive (although it doesn’t produce any more healing berries). If activated elsewhere, it withers and dies within 1d4 days. Item 1 Feather Token (Ladder) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 3 gp When activated, this feather transforms permanently into a 20-foot-long wooden ladder. Item 8 Feather Token (Swan Boat) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 76 gp This feather can be activated only when tossed into a large body of water, such as a lake or broad river. It transforms into a swan-shaped boat capable of carrying up to 32 Medium creatures, 8 Large creatures, or 2 Huge creatures. The boat moves on the water at a Speed of 50 feet, and lasts 1 day. Item 6 Feather Token (Tree) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 38 gp This token can be activated only on an unoccupied patch of earth or soil. When activated, this token transforms into an oak tree, 60 feet tall with a 5-foot-wide trunk. The tree continues to live and grow if conditions are favorable. Item 9 Feather Token (Whip) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 130 gp This feather transforms into a +1 striking dancing whip when activated. The whip immediately jumps from your grasp and proceeds to attack your enemies until 1 minute has passed or it fails its flat check for dancing , at which point it vanishes. If the whip’s target isn’t prone, the whip uses its actions to attempt to Trip that creature instead of making a Strike. The whip’s total attack modifier for Striking or Tripping is +18 instead of the normal bonus for a dancing weapon. Item 6 Feather Token (Balloon) Source Pathfinder Special: Fumbus Price 50 gp This feather can't be activated underwater. When activated, the feather transforms into a balloon of waxed cloth that is 3 feet in diameter and filled with hot air. Handles on the bottom of the balloon allow up to two creatures sized Medium or smaller to hold onto the balloon. One round after being activated, the balloon rises up into the air at a speed of 20 feet per round. After rising for 3 rounds, the balloon floats in place for two rounds as the air inside cools, then descends at a speed of 20 feet per round. When the balloon reaches its original elevation, the balloon deflates. Item 3 Feather Token (Puddle) Source Pathfinder Special: Fumbus Price 8 gp When activated, the feather transforms into two gallons of fresh, clear water. If no one drinks it, the water evaporates after 1 day.

fields.text: Item 1+ Feather Token Conjuration Consumable Magical Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Activate Single Action Interact Each feather token appears to be a simple feather from some exotic bird. The feather’s shaft, dipped in gold, bears a single arcane rune. Activating a feather token causes it to transform into another object, which then can be used as normal for that object. Each feather can be activated only once, with most of them permanently becoming the item in their description. Item 7 Feather Token (Anchor) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 55 gp This feather can be activated only on a boat. When activated, this feather transforms into a massive anchor that causes the boat to immediately stop. After 1 day, the anchor vanishes and the boat can move as normal. The anchor is attached to the boat by a magical chain of force, but the chain can be removed by dispel magic or destroyed (Hardness 30, HP 40). Item 3 Feather Token (Bird) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 8 gp When activated, this token transforms into a small sparrow that waits on your finger for you to relay a message up to 1 minute in length, along with the name and rough location of a recipient. The recipient must be someone you have met, and the location must be somewhere you have visited. After receiving the message, the bird flies off to deliver it, traveling at 30 miles per hour and then searching for the target in the location you provided. If the bird finds the target, it moves adjacent to them, your words emanate from the bird, and the bird then flies off and vanishes. The bird also vanishes if it fails to find your target after 10 hours of searching the location you specified. Item 3 Feather Token (Chest) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 10 gp When you use this token, a small wooden chest appears and immediately opens. This chest can hold up to 10 Bulk worth of items. Once the chest is closed, it transforms again—this time into a key—taking all of the stored items with it. You can activate this key by spending an Interact action to turn it in an imaginary lock, which causes it to transform back into a chest with all of the items still inside. Once it has turned into a chest a second time, it forever remains a wooden chest. Item 4 Feather Token (Fan) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 15 gp Activating this feather requires you to fan it in a given direction. If this direction is toward the sail of a vessel, the feather flutters up toward the sail and fans continuously, filling the sail with air and granting the vessel a +10-foot circumstance bonus to its Speed for 8 hours. If fanned in any other direction, it instead produces a single casting of gust of wind (DC 20). Item 2 Feather Token (Holly Bush) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 6 gp When this feather is activated, it immediately transforms into a living holly bush, filling a single square. This bush can provide standard cover. In addition, the bush has 2d4 bright-red berries. While holly berries are usually poisonous, these berries are infused with beneficial magic. You can pick and eat a berry as an Interact action to recover 1 Hit Point. Once plucked from the bush, a berry becomes non-magical after a few seconds, so it doesn’t heal you if you don’t eat it within the span of your Interact action. If activated on soil, the plant continues to grow and thrive (although it doesn’t produce any more healing berries). If activated elsewhere, it withers and dies within 1d4 days. Item 1 Feather Token (Ladder) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 3 gp When activated, this feather transforms permanently into a 20-foot-long wooden ladder. Item 8 Feather Token (Swan Boat) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 76 gp This feather can be activated only when tossed into a large body of water, such as a lake or broad river. It transforms into a swan-shaped boat capable of carrying up to 32 Medium creatures, 8 Large creatures, or 2 Huge creatures. The boat moves on the water at a Speed of 50 feet, and lasts 1 day. Item 6 Feather Token (Tree) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 38 gp This token can be activated only on an unoccupied patch of earth or soil. When activated, this token transforms into an oak tree, 60 feet tall with a 5-foot-wide trunk. The tree continues to live and grow if conditions are favorable. Item 9 Feather Token (Whip) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 130 gp This feather transforms into a +1 striking dancing whip when activated. The whip immediately jumps from your grasp and proceeds to attack your enemies until 1 minute has passed or it fails its flat check for dancing , at which point it vanishes. If the whip’s target isn’t prone, the whip uses its actions to attempt to Trip that creature instead of making a Strike. The whip’s total attack modifier for Striking or Tripping is +18 instead of the normal bonus for a dancing weapon. Item 6 Feather Token (Balloon) Source Pathfinder Special: Fumbus Price 50 gp This feather can't be activated underwater. When activated, the feather transforms into a balloon of waxed cloth that is 3 feet in diameter and filled with hot air. Handles on the bottom of the balloon allow up to two creatures sized Medium or smaller to hold onto the balloon. One round after being activated, the balloon rises up into the air at a speed of 20 feet per round. After rising for 3 rounds, the balloon floats in place for two rounds as the air inside cools, then descends at a speed of 20 feet per round. When the balloon reaches its original elevation, the balloon deflates. Item 3 Feather Token (Puddle) Source Pathfinder Special: Fumbus Price 8 gp When activated, the feather transforms into two gallons of fresh, clear water. If no one drinks it, the water evaporates after 1 day.

fields.text: Item 1+ Feather Token Conjuration Consumable Magical Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Activate Single Action Interact Each feather token appears to be a simple feather from some exotic bird. The feather’s shaft, dipped in gold, bears a single arcane rune. Activating a feather token causes it to transform into another object, which then can be used as normal for that object. Each feather can be activated only once, with most of them permanently becoming the item in their description. Item 7 Feather Token (Anchor) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 55 gp This feather can be activated only on a boat. When activated, this feather transforms into a massive anchor that causes the boat to immediately stop. After 1 day, the anchor vanishes and the boat can move as normal. The anchor is attached to the boat by a magical chain of force, but the chain can be removed by dispel magic or destroyed (Hardness 30, HP 40). Item 3 Feather Token (Bird) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 8 gp When activated, this token transforms into a small sparrow that waits on your finger for you to relay a message up to 1 minute in length, along with the name and rough location of a recipient. The recipient must be someone you have met, and the location must be somewhere you have visited. After receiving the message, the bird flies off to deliver it, traveling at 30 miles per hour and then searching for the target in the location you provided. If the bird finds the target, it moves adjacent to them, your words emanate from the bird, and the bird then flies off and vanishes. The bird also vanishes if it fails to find your target after 10 hours of searching the location you specified. Item 3 Feather Token (Chest) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 10 gp When you use this token, a small wooden chest appears and immediately opens. This chest can hold up to 10 Bulk worth of items. Once the chest is closed, it transforms again—this time into a key—taking all of the stored items with it. You can activate this key by spending an Interact action to turn it in an imaginary lock, which causes it to transform back into a chest with all of the items still inside. Once it has turned into a chest a second time, it forever remains a wooden chest. Item 4 Feather Token (Fan) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 15 gp Activating this feather requires you to fan it in a given direction. If this direction is toward the sail of a vessel, the feather flutters up toward the sail and fans continuously, filling the sail with air and granting the vessel a +10-foot circumstance bonus to its Speed for 8 hours. If fanned in any other direction, it instead produces a single casting of gust of wind (DC 20). Item 2 Feather Token (Holly Bush) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 6 gp When this feather is activated, it immediately transforms into a living holly bush, filling a single square. This bush can provide standard cover. In addition, the bush has 2d4 bright-red berries. While holly berries are usually poisonous, these berries are infused with beneficial magic. You can pick and eat a berry as an Interact action to recover 1 Hit Point. Once plucked from the bush, a berry becomes non-magical after a few seconds, so it doesn’t heal you if you don’t eat it within the span of your Interact action. If activated on soil, the plant continues to grow and thrive (although it doesn’t produce any more healing berries). If activated elsewhere, it withers and dies within 1d4 days. Item 1 Feather Token (Ladder) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 3 gp When activated, this feather transforms permanently into a 20-foot-long wooden ladder. Item 8 Feather Token (Swan Boat) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 76 gp This feather can be activated only when tossed into a large body of water, such as a lake or broad river. It transforms into a swan-shaped boat capable of carrying up to 32 Medium creatures, 8 Large creatures, or 2 Huge creatures. The boat moves on the water at a Speed of 50 feet, and lasts 1 day. Item 6 Feather Token (Tree) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 38 gp This token can be activated only on an unoccupied patch of earth or soil. When activated, this token transforms into an oak tree, 60 feet tall with a 5-foot-wide trunk. The tree continues to live and grow if conditions are favorable. Item 9 Feather Token (Whip) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 130 gp This feather transforms into a +1 striking dancing whip when activated. The whip immediately jumps from your grasp and proceeds to attack your enemies until 1 minute has passed or it fails its flat check for dancing , at which point it vanishes. If the whip’s target isn’t prone, the whip uses its actions to attempt to Trip that creature instead of making a Strike. The whip’s total attack modifier for Striking or Tripping is +18 instead of the normal bonus for a dancing weapon. Item 6 Feather Token (Balloon) Source Pathfinder Special: Fumbus Price 50 gp This feather can't be activated underwater. When activated, the feather transforms into a balloon of waxed cloth that is 3 feet in diameter and filled with hot air. Handles on the bottom of the balloon allow up to two creatures sized Medium or smaller to hold onto the balloon. One round after being activated, the balloon rises up into the air at a speed of 20 feet per round. After rising for 3 rounds, the balloon floats in place for two rounds as the air inside cools, then descends at a speed of 20 feet per round. When the balloon reaches its original elevation, the balloon deflates. Item 3 Feather Token (Puddle) Source Pathfinder Special: Fumbus Price 8 gp When activated, the feather transforms into two gallons of fresh, clear water. If no one drinks it, the water evaporates after 1 day.

Item 7 Feather Token (Anchor) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 55 gp This feather can be activated only on a boat. When activated, this feather transforms into a massive anchor that causes the boat to immediately stop. After 1 day, the anchor vanishes and the boat can move as normal. The anchor is attached to the boat by a magical chain of force, but the chain can be removed by dispel magic or destroyed (Hardness 30, HP 40). Item 3 Feather Token (Bird) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 8 gp When activated, this token transforms into a small sparrow that waits on your finger for you to relay a message up to 1 minute in length, along with the name and rough location of a recipient. The recipient must be someone you have met, and the location must be somewhere you have visited. After receiving the message, the bird flies off to deliver it, traveling at 30 miles per hour and then searching for the target in the location you provided. If the bird finds the target, it moves adjacent to them, your words emanate from the bird, and the bird then flies off and vanishes. The bird also vanishes if it fails to find your target after 10 hours of searching the location you specified. Item 3 Feather Token (Chest) Source Core Rulebook pg. 570 Price 10 gp When you use this token, a small wooden chest appears and immediately opens. This chest can hold up to 10 Bulk worth of items. Once the chest is closed, it transforms again—this time into a key—taking all of the stored items with it. While holly berries are usually poisonous, these berries are infused with beneficial magic. You can pick and eat a berry as an Interact action to recover 1 Hit Point. Once plucked from the bush, a berry becomes non-magical after a few seconds, so it doesn’t heal you if you don’t eat it within the span of your Interact action.

 If activated on soil, the plant continues to grow and thrive (although it doesn’t produce any more healing berries). If activated elsewhere, it withers and dies within 1d4 days.

Once the chest is closed, it transforms again—this time into a key—taking all of the stored items with it. You can activate this key by spending an Interact action to turn it in an imaginary lock, which causes it to transform back into a chest with all of the items still inside. Once it has turned into a chest a second time, it forever remains a wooden chest.

Activating this feather requires you to fan it in a given direction. If this direction is toward the sail of a vessel, the feather flutters up toward the sail and fans continuously, filling the sail with air and granting the vessel a +10-foot circumstance bonus to its Speed for 8 hours. If fanned in any other direction, it instead produces a single casting of [_gust of wind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=143) (DC 20).

When this feather is activated, it immediately transforms into a living holly bush, filling a single square. This bush can provide standard cover. In addition, the bush has 2d4 bright-red berries. While holly berries are usually poisonous, these berries are infused with beneficial magic. You can pick and eat a berry as an Interact action to recover 1 Hit Point. Once plucked from the bush, a berry becomes non-magical after a few seconds, so it doesn’t heal you if you don’t eat it within the span of your Interact action.

 If activated on soil, the plant continues to grow and thrive (although it doesn’t produce any more healing berries). If activated elsewhere, it withers and dies within 1d4 days.

The whip immediately jumps from your grasp and proceeds to attack your enemies until 1 minute has passed or it fails its flat check for _dancing_, at which point it vanishes. Elven archers were the first to create the _featherlight fletching_, meant for long-range battles, though artisans of many other ancestries have now learned the art of crafting these whetstones. A _featherlight fletching_ is a feather-shaped trinket crafted of spun silver filigree and aids projectiles in flying true, even over great distances. A ranged weapon under the effects of a _featherlight fletching_ doubles its range increment for 1 minute.

</title>

<traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #194: Cult of the Cave Worm](/Sources.aspx?ID=209) pg. 79

**Price** 230 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The book's cover is a patchwork of tanned [humanoid](/Traits.aspx?ID=91) skin that reeks of rotting meat. The longer a living creature studies this book, the more the scent of decay appeals to them.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** Your last action was to cast a necromancy spell prepared from this grimoire;  **Effect** You draw negative energy from the triggering spell. You gain 10 temporary hit points that last for 1 hour.

---

 **Special** If this grimoire is used to prepare spells five days in succession by the same caster, that caster is subjected to the [curse of the ravenous](/Curses.aspx?ID=19).

---

This long bar has two cuffs that enclose a prisoner's ankles or wrists. Fetters apply a –20-foot circumstance penalty to Speed and disrupt any manipulate action the bound creature attempts unless it succeeds at a DC 11 flat check. Freeing a creature from simple fetters requires 2 successful DC 23 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) checks. Average fetters require 3 successful DC 28 Thievery checks, good fetters require 4 successful DC 33 Thievery checks, and superior fetters require 5 successful DC 43 Thievery checks.

Freeing a creature from simple fetters requires 2 successful DC 23 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) checks. Average fetters require 3 successful DC 28 Thievery checks, good fetters require 4 successful DC 33 Thievery checks, and superior fetters require 5 successful DC 43 Thievery checks.

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 238 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 1 --- Vines twine around this wooden staff, carved with silhouettes of [pixies](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3212) and [nymphs](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=449). Some _fey staves_ have the symbol of an [Eldest](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=7) inlaid in silver on their surfaces. While wielding the staff, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) and [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks against creatures with the [fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=599) trait. **Activate** Cast a Spell **Effect** You expend a number of charges from the staff to cast a spell from its list. **Craft Requirements** Supply one casting of all listed ranks of all listed spells.   • **Cantrip** [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1485)
  • **1st** [_charm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1463), [_summon fey_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1700)
  • **2nd** [_entangling flora_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1515), [_mist_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1606), _summon fey_

  • **5th** [_incarnate faerie revelers_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2740), _summon fey_, [_tree of life and death_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2851)

To creatures other than fey, the scent of feyfoul seems to be a faint but non-obnoxious odor of cinnamon, but fey find that the stuff interferes with their ability to manipulate a creature's mind. Jubilost invented feyfoul accidentally while he was attempting to create a cologne that would enhance its wearer's appearance to make them seem more otherworldly, but to anyone that asks, the gnome alchemist quickly claims that he'd always intended to create an alchemical tool that provided protection from fey magic.

 A single dose of feyfoul spritzed on a person in the manner of perfume grants the wearer an item bonus to Will saving throws against [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) effects generated by [fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=69) creatures.

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 136 **Price** 10,000 gp **Usage** held in 2 hands **Bulk** L --- This exquisite fiddle is perfectly carved and balanced to produce the purest sound while granting its player perfect balance and poise. It grants a +2 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) checks. If you’re a master in Performance, while playing it you also gain a +1 status bonus to Reflex saves and a +1 item bonus to Dexterity-based skill checks. If you’re legendary in Performance, the bonuses are +2. When you [Perform](/Actions.aspx?ID=2401) with the fiddle, you can choose to create a harsh and discordant note. You critically fail the Performance check, shred the strings of the fiddle, and create an 8th-rank [_noise blast_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1616), with a 40-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) around you instead of a 10-foot [burst](/Rules.aspx?ID=2385). The fiddle can’t be played again until the strings are replaced at a cost of 200 gp. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Effect** You expend a number of charges from this instrument to cast a spell from its list.
  • **Cantrip** [_figment_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1528), [_light_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1585), [_message_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1598)
  • **1st** [_command_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1470)
  • **2nd** [_calm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1458), [_revealing light_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1653)
  • **3rd** [_enthrall_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1516)
  • **4th** [_honeyed words_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1558)
  • **5th** [_sending_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1665)
  • **6th** _calm_, [_dominate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1501), [_vibrant pattern_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1741)
  • **7th** _dominate_, [_mask of terror_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1595), [_true target_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1726), _vibrant pattern_, [_visions of danger_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2040)
**Craft Requirements** Supply one casting of all listed levels of all listed spells.

fields.text: Item 16 Fiddle of the Maestro Rare Coda Enchantment Occult Staff Source Treasure Vault pg. 136 Price 10,000 gp Usage held in 2 hands Bulk L This exquisite fiddle is perfectly carved and balanced to produce the purest sound while granting its player perfect balance and poise. It grants a +2 item bonus to Performance checks. If you’re a master in Performance, while playing it you also gain a +1 status bonus to Reflex saves and a +1 item bonus to Dexterity-based skill checks. If you’re legendary in Performance, the bonuses are +2. When you Perform with the fiddle, you can choose to create a harsh and discordant note. You critically fail the Performance check, shred the strings of the fiddle, and create an 8th-level sound burst , with a 40-foot emanation around you instead of a 10-foot burst. The fiddle can’t be played again until the strings are replaced at a cost of 200 gp. Activate Cast a Spell; Effect You expend a number of charges from this instrument to cast a spell from its list. ---

Many cultures of Golarion have a tattoo that is believed to turn away harm. As such, _warding tattoos_ often resemble whichever dangers are most common to the culture, such as a wild beast in the forests of Kyonin, a whirlpool in the high seas of the Shackles, or the stylized face of a [demon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=387) in the Sarkoris Scar. 

**Activate—Inked Safeguard** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** An enemy, hazard, or the environment makes an attack against your AC, requires you to attempt a saving throw, or causes you to take damage automatically;  **Effect** Until the end of the current turn, against the triggering effect, you gain a +1 status bonus to AC and saving throws and gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) 2 to the triggering damage.

As she sought to forge alliances with other lands surrounding her own, Jininsiel crafted potent magic items as gifts. For the people of Tianjing, she created this staff, which served the people of that nation well for many years. They returned it to Jinin as a token of condolence when that nation’s leader passed into the Great Beyond. Many centuries later, when the people of Jinin learned that their kin had returned to Kyonin from Castrovel only to face fiendish threats in their homeland, a group of priests from Jinin traveled across the world to help. They brought with them _Fiendbreaker_ and chose to leave it in Kyonin to help protect them in the future from [demonic](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=387) foes. _Fiendbreaker_ functions as a _[+2 greater striking ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [holy](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2842) standard-grade [cold iron ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2916) [staff](/Weapons.aspx?ID=367)_. May contain spoilers from Spore War **Source** [Pathfinder #212: A Voice in the Blight](/Sources.aspx?ID=255) pg. 72 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 1 --- **Perception** +35; precise [low-light vision](/Rules.aspx?ID=2411) and hearing within 30 feet **Communication** [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) (partner only) **Skills** [Demon Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +33, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +34, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) +35 **Int** +5, **Wis** +7, **Cha** +6 **Will** +35 --- The stately echo of Jininsiel, the woman who guided her people through the Darklands to escape the devastation of Earthfall, causes _Fiendbreaker_ to softly shimmer with a silvery radiance equivalent to that of candlelight. _Fiendbreaker_ can activate or deactivate this radiance as a free action once per round on her partner’s turn. _Fiendbreaker’s_ telepathic voice is calm and soothing, seeking to support her partner’s decisions with compliments or warnings against overconfidence as needed. _Fiendbreaker_ functions as a _[+3 major striking ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [holy ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2842) [high-grade cold iron ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2916) [staff](/Weapons.aspx?ID=367)_. While wielding the staff, you gain a +3 circumstance bonus to checks to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about any sort of [fiend](/Traits.aspx?ID=600). **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** You expend a number of charges from the staff to cast a spell from her list. _Fiendbreaker_ can use this activation only if you’re holding the staff and only if you haven’t used Fiendbreaker to Cast a Spell this round. Likewise, if _Fiendbreaker_ Casts a Spell from the staff, you can’t activate the staff to Cast a Spell this round.
  • **Cantrip** [_divine lance_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1498)
  • **1st** [_sanctuary_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1660)
  • **2nd** [see the unseen](/Feats.aspx?ID=2815)
  • **3rd** [_anointed ground_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1965), [_holy light_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1557)
  • **4th** [_clear mind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1469), [_planar tether_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1636)
  • **5th** [_banishment_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1448), [_divine wrath_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1499)
  • **6th** _holy light_, [_spirit blast_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1685)
  • **7th** [_divine decree_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1495), [_planar seal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1635)
  • **8th** _divine wrath_, _holy light_
  • **9th** _banishment _, _divine decree_
**Activate—Restore Mind** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Effect** _Fiendbreaker_ attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) an ongoing mental affect you’re suffering from, with a counteract rank of 9th and a +25 modifier to the roll (or a +30 modifier if the source of the [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effect on you was created by a [fiend](/Traits.aspx?ID=600)). _Nethys Note: the non-artifact version of the item is [here.](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3698) This artifact's heroic legacy, and its subsequent skills and ability attribute, are presented [here](/Rules.aspx?ID=3419). _

Fiendbreaker can use this activation only if you’re holding the staff and only if you haven’t used Fiendbreaker to Cast a Spell this round. A Large or smaller restrained or willing creature can be executed by a _final blade_. 

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 1 minute (Interact);     **Effect** You execute a creature restrained beneath the blade. The creature you execute takes 11d10 slashing damage and must succeed at a DC 45 Fortitude save or be decapitated as though it suffered a critical hit with a natural 20 from a _+3 major striking [vorpal](/Equipment.aspx?ID=308)_ scythe. The soul of a creature executed with a _final blade_ is trapped, and the creature can't be returned to life, not even by [_miracle_](/Spells.aspx?ID=196) or similar magic. A _final blade_ can hold any number of souls in this way, and a sufficient number of captured souls forms a monster called a [gray death](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1641).

fields.text: Item 18 Final Rest Magical Necromancy Source Book of the Dead pg. 19 Price 24,000 gp Usage held in 1 hand Bulk 1 Base Weapon Longsword This +3 greater disrupting greater striking silver longsword is made from the purest silver. The blade is carefully etched to depict a vast and sprawling necropolis, a place where the dead are laid to rest. Whenever you critically hit an undead creature with final rest , the undead creature takes 3d6 persistent good damage, with a DC 36 Fortitude save. Critical Success No effect. Success The creature takes half the persistent good damage. Failure The creature is stunned 1 and takes the full persistent good damage. Critical Failure The creature is stunned 3 and takes double the persistent good damage. Activate Two Actions command, envision; Frequency once per day; Effect You hold the sword aloft, making it cast sunburst (DC 38 Reflex save). Craft Requirements The initial raw materials must include 4,950 gp of silver.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 20"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Final Scalecloak](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3508)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=723" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=537" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 151

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn cloak

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Fashioned from a swath of Mogaru’s red-and-black hide and trimmed with Agyra’s rough scales in green, blue, and white, this cloak draws upon the power of both kaiju, but at considerable cost. Any [kaiju](/Traits.aspx?ID=383) within a 5-mile radius of the Final Scalecloak can sense the presence and nature of the item, and can also determine whether it’s being worn by a mortal. This sense grows stronger as the item and kaiju near one another, until the kaiju can pinpoint exactly where the cloak is and who currently possesses it.

When worn, the Final Scalecloak grants you [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) 15 to physical and precision damage, [immunity](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) to [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), and a [Fly speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2350) of 60 feet. You are unaffected by strong winds while flying. 

**Activate—Commune with Kaiju** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320); you gain the effects of a 6th-rank [_telepathy_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1719) spell but can use it only to communicate with Gargantuan [animals](/Traits.aspx?ID=531) and [beasts](/Traits.aspx?ID=547). Most kaiju are [hostile](/Conditions.aspx?ID=80) toward you for wearing the Final Scalecloak, however, requiring great effort to calm them enough to have a conversation.

**Activate—Embody the Storm** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320); a nimbus of crackling electricity surrounds you for 1 minute. You gain a +4 status bonus to AC against ranged projectiles that are at least partly made of metal. If a foe attempts to [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) you with an unarmed attack or melee attack with a weapon at least partly made of metal, that creature takes 3d10 [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586) damage ([basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) DC 40 Reflex save).

**Destruction** The Final Scalecloak is torn to shreds if the wearer is struck by an attack or effect from both Agyra and Mogaru within the same round.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Final Stand](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3844)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 127

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Rapier](/Weapons.aspx?ID=391)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The origins of this _[+3 greater striking ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [rapier](/Weapons.aspx?ID=391)_ are shrouded in mystery, but it earned its name in the hands of an unknown hero who used it to singlehandedly defend a remote Nirmathi village from a vicious gang of bandits, shrugging off dozens of blows that would have felled any other mortal. Only when all of the bandits had been dispatched or driven off did the noble warrior finally succumb to their injuries.

While wielding _Final Stand_, if you take damage that would reduce you to 0 Hit Points but not immediately kill you, attempt a DC 11 [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333). If you succeed, you avoid being knocked out and remain at 1 Hit Point instead. For the remainder of the encounter, you can’t regain Hit Points in any way, though you can be stabilized if you gain the [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) condition. If you’re still conscious and there are no nearby enemies that you can perceive, you immediately drop to 0 Hit Points and are dying 1. If you have any other abilities that would allow you to remain at 1 Hit Point when you would be reduced to 0 Hit Points (such as [Orc Ferocity](/Feats.aspx?ID=4514)), you must use those abilities before you can benefit from _Final Stand’s_ ability.

**Destruction** If the wielder of _Final Stand_ surrenders to their enemies while any of their allies are still standing, the blade weakens and the DC of the flat check permanently increases by 2. Final Stand shatters into hundreds of pieces the moment the DC of the flat check is ever higher than 20.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 3"
    pfs=""
>
[Fingerprinting Kit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=797)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Agents of Edgewatch</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #157: Devil at the Dreaming Palace](/Sources.aspx?ID=45) pg. 77

**Price** 30 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Hands** 2

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Rarely found outside of major metropolises, fingerprinting kits are a state-of-the-art, non-magical means of linking suspects to the scene of a crime.

 The kit consists of two parts. The first, a delicate brush and a jar of extremely fine dust, is used to reveal fingerprints left behind by most humanoid creatures. The dust sticks to the natural oils left behind on smooth surfaces. When you use the kit to determine whether or not creatures left behind a fingerprint at a crime scene, the GM rolls a [secret](/Traits.aspx?ID=142) [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) check against the Thievery DC of every creature capable of leaving prints that has interacted with the scene. On a success, you locate a clear print from that creature and carefully transfer it to a special sheet of sticky paper. (Note that fingerprints can last for days, and prints collected in this manner often include those of victims, witnesses, and unrelated passersby.) At the GM's discretion, the print-leaving creature might get a bonus to its Thievery DC for taking special precautions. In other cases, finding a print might be impossible (such as if the creature was wearing gloves or if the location has been significantly compromised).

 The second part of the kit is a small sheaf of paper and a pad soaked in ink. By forcing a humanoid creature with fingerprints to roll a finger across the pad and then press it to the paper, you can obtain an image of the unique whorls in that creature's fingerprints. These can then be compared to any prints found at a crime scene. Successfully determining whether or not two prints match requires a DC 15 Perception check—the GM should roll this check secretly as well, since a failed check may result in false information.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

Fiery Anulite paprika, sunrise cinnamon, and winterbite are hidden inside this salad's translucent leaves, bringing the cool of snow and the heat of steam to every bite. The dueling sensations make some diners sweat and others shiver, but all leave with a lasting sense of heat and cold that make other sources pale in comparison. When you consume the salad, you gain resistance 5 to [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) and [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27) for 1 minute.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Monsters of Myth](/Sources.aspx?ID=107) pg. 112 **Price** 15 gp --- You carefully pack rare, heat-absorbing powders into a specially prepared clay vessel, then bury the vessel in the ground up to its neck. When a creature enters the square, the vessel's neck shatters, dispersing the powders into the air. The powder instantly douses non-magical fires the size of a campfire or smaller within 10 feet of the snare. The creature triggering the snare must attempt a DC 20 Reflex save to avoid getting powder in its face. A creature [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1) or [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) by the powder can use an Interact action to attempt a DC 10 flat check; on a success, it removes the condition. On a failure, it can try again, with a DC of 5 on the next Interact check. If it fails a second time, it automatically removes the condition with a third Interact action. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is dazzled for 1 round.
**Failure** The creature is blinded until the end of its next turn and dazzled for 1 minute afterwards.
**Critical Failure** The creature is blinded for 1 minute and dazzled for 10 minutes afterwards.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Fire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=604" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 310

**Price** 940 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This black, metal ring is inset with rubies that occasionally give off wisps of smoke. It grants you a +2 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks.

**Activate—Fire Jump** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2229), [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You Stride (or Burrow or Fly, if you have the corresponding Speed) into any fire large enough to contain you, including magical fires. You vanish into the fire and take no damage from it. You can sense all sufficiently large fires within 100 feet of where you vanish, and you reemerge from any of those fires, either within the fire or adjacent to it. If you end your movement in the fire, it affects you as normal.

fields.text: Item 0 Firearm Cleaning Kit Uncommon Source Guns & Gears pg. 179 PFS Note Characters with access to a firearm also automatically are granted access to the firearm cleaning kit. Price 1 sp Hands 2 Bulk L This kit contains cleaning cloth, oil, small steel brushes, and other minor tools necessary for proper cleaning and maintenance of a firearm. Without a firearm cleaning kit, you can’t perform the necessary tasks during your daily preparations to ensure that your firearm isn’t at risk of misfiring under normal use conditions.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Firefoot Popcorn](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1916)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 48

**Price** 75 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

When you consume firefoot popcorn, for 1 minute, you can [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=81) double the normal distance. You can also attempt to [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=36) or [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=37) as a single action. If you do, you don't perform the initial Stride (nor do you fall if you don't Stride 10 feet).

 Each time you Leap 10 feet or more, your feet make a popping sound that can be heard from at least 100 feet, and the space you left fills with waves of intense heat. For 1 minute, that square is [hazardous terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=454) that deals 1d6 fire damage to any creature that moves into it.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 9+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Fireproof Gloves](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3963)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 149

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn gloves

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

First developed by blacksmiths to move burning hot workpieces around, _fireproof gloves_ then became popular with soldiers responsible for disabling bombs and magical traps. The thick tan gloves come up over the arm. When wearing these gloves, you gain fire [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) 5.

**Activate—Release Heat** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** You have a free hand; **Effect** You take the heat that’s built up in your gloves and discharge it onto an enemy. You deal 6d8 fire damage to one creature within reach (DC 26 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

Greater Fireproof Gloves

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 170 **Usage** affixed to armor or a weapon --- Identical feathers radiate from the center of this spellheart, held in place by woven straw. The spell attack roll of any spell cast by Activating this item is +8, and the spell DC is 18.
  • **Armor** You gain a +1 item bonus to [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) checks and resistance 2 to falling damage.
  • **Weapon** After you cast an [air](/Traits.aspx?ID=5) spell by Activating the wreath, you can Fly 5 feet as a single action, or you can Fly 10 feet as a free action if the spell you cast wasn't a cantrip. This must be your next action, and if you don't have a fly Speed, you must end the flight on solid ground or fall.
**Activate** Cast a Spell; **Effect** You cast [_gale blast_](/Spells.aspx?ID=917). Five-Feather Wreath **Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 170 **Price** 90 gp Five-Feather Wreath (Greater) **Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 170 **Price** 425 gp --- Resistance when affixed to armor is 5, fly distance affixed to a weapon casting a non-cantrip spell is 25 feet, the spell attack roll is +14, and spell DC is 24. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You cast [_wall of wind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=367). Five-Feather Wreath (Major) **Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 170 **Price** 1,750 gp --- Bonus affixed to armor is +2, resistance when affixed to armor is 10, fly distance affixed to a weapon casting a non-cantrip spell is 40 feet, spell attack roll is +19, and spell DC is 29. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You cast 4th-level [_wall of wind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=367). **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You cast [_air walk_](/Spells.aspx?ID=6).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 0+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Fixer](/Equipment.aspx?ID=879)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 116

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A fixer is a guide who knows the inner workings of life in a given location. The right fixer can help you navigate the complicated alleyways of a new city or the tangled social expectations of the local populace. Every fixer has knowledge about a specific location, such as a settlement like Katapesh, a geographical region like the Verduran Forest, or a notable establishment like the Grand Lodge. If you plan to hire a fixer, you must do so for the specific location for which you need a guide, though the GM can decide that a given fixer may be able to provide assistance with a closely related location, such as a fixer for the Isle of Kortos being able to provide some guidance for the town of Diobel.

 There are two varieties of fixers: informants and counselors. Informants help provide basic information on a location, such as how to navigate a city, the type of animals native to a region, or the type of clothing worn by specific members of a local thieves' guild. An informant automatically [Aids](/Actions.aspx?ID=75) you on attempts to [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=49) and [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) about your specific location, granting you a +1 circumstance bonus to such checks. An expert informant critically succeeds at Aiding you, granting a +2 circumstance bonus.

 A counselor is specialized in social matters. They can help you learn proper etiquette, introduce you to important or useful people, and generally help navigate social circles. A counselor automatically Aids you on attempts to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46), [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=47), [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50), and [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=51) when speaking with individuals within the location of the counselor's expertise. An expert counselor critically succeeds at Aiding you, granting a +2 circumstance bonus.

 The GM is the final arbiter in deciding whether or a not a fixer for a given location is available. A fixer's rate may also change depending on the location or the nature of guidance required. For example, a fixer might lower their rate for simple guidance, such as locating the best Qadiran cuisine in Absalom, or increase their rate when dealing with dangerous information or individuals, such as helping navigate a sewer inhabited by dangerous monsters. Pathfinders are typically able to hire a fixer without issue, but must do so through contacts at a local lodge.

<row gap="medium">

---

A fixer is a guide who knows the inner workings of life in a given location. The right fixer can help you navigate the complicated alleyways of a new city or the tangled social expectations of the local populace. Every fixer has knowledge about a specific location, such as a settlement like Katapesh, a geographical region like the Verduran Forest, or a notable establishment like the Grand Lodge. If you plan to hire a fixer, you must do so for the specific location for which you need a guide, though the GM can decide that a given fixer may be able to provide assistance with a closely related location, such as a fixer for the Isle of Kortos being able to provide some guidance for the town of Diobel.

 There are two varieties of fixers: informants and counselors. Informants help provide basic information on a location, such as how to navigate a city, the type of animals native to a region, or the type of clothing worn by specific members of a local thieves' guild. An informant automatically [Aids](/Actions.aspx?ID=75) you on attempts to [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=49) and [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) about your specific location, granting you a +1 circumstance bonus to such checks. An expert informant critically succeeds at Aiding you, granting a +2 circumstance bonus.

 A counselor is specialized in social matters. They can help you learn proper etiquette, introduce you to important or useful people, and generally help navigate social circles. A counselor automatically Aids you on attempts to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46), [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=47), [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50), and [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=51) when speaking with individuals within the location of the counselor's expertise. An expert counselor critically succeeds at Aiding you, granting a +2 circumstance bonus.

 The GM is the final arbiter in deciding whether or a not a fixer for a given location is available. A fixer's rate may also change depending on the location or the nature of guidance required. For example, a fixer might lower their rate for simple guidance, such as locating the best Qadiran cuisine in Absalom, or increase their rate when dealing with dangerous information or individuals, such as helping navigate a sewer inhabited by dangerous monsters. Pathfinders are typically able to hire a fixer without issue, but must do so through contacts at a local lodge.

</title>

<traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 79

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) All Pathfinder Society agents have access to all uncommon clockwork items and gadgets from Chapters 1 and 2 of this book_

**Price** 25 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

**Access** Characters from Absalom, New Thassilon, Alkenstar, Dongun Hold, or especially technological regions of Arcadia like the Deadshot Lands have access to uncommon clockwork items from the first two chapters of this book.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

The snare takes the form of a Tiny, [drake](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=36)-like clockwork toy. When a creature enters its square the snare activates, causing the drake to spit a gout of fire in a 15-foot cone in the direction from which the creature entered. For instance, if a creature entered the square coming from the east, the cone would point east, to hit any allies behind the triggering creature. Those within the cone must succeed a DC 19 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save or take 6d6 fire damage. After spitting its fire, the snare falls apart.

---

Slathering this reddish-gold balm over a suit of armor creates a swirling pattern of flame-like licks and curls. </title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Dead God's Hand</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=537" />

<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=579" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [The Dead God's Hand](/Sources.aspx?ID=370) pg. 144

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

**_Nethys Note: This artifact contains spoilers for The Dead God's Hand. Read at your own risk._**

The ancient lost artifact known as the _Radiant Spark_ could bestow its flames upon the wick of any candle, after which the electric-blue flame would burn eternally until it is activated or the candle itself is jostled enough to move it (see Destruction below).

 You activate a flame of the _Radiant Spark_ either by using your fingers to extinguish the flame or by blowing it out, causing the crackling blue energy to leap into your body and then settle in one of your hands. The blue flame continues to burn harmlessly on your hand, shedding illumination equivalent to a candle, and it can be extinguished only by your death or by expending it through calling upon the flame's power to cast a 6th-rank _[raise dead](/Spells.aspx?ID=1645)_ to your specifications. You can hold only one flame of the _Radiant Spark_ at a time—if you activate another flame before your current one is extinguished, the new flame replaces the previous one. The PCs can get a hint at how to use the flames of the _Radiant Spark_ in Sarnax's Tomb by deduction, as well as by careful study of the _Radiant Spark_ wall panel at area **B8**.

**Destruction** While the _Radiant Spark_ itself is nearly as indestructible as any other artifact, these flames created by its power are fragile. A candle bearing a flame of the _Radiant Spark_ can burn forever, but any attempt to move the candle (including any accidental toppling over caused by nearby events) causes the flame to gutter. The flame can still be claimed if someone extinguishes it with their fingers within a minute, otherwise the flame goes out. Curiously, wind and water cannot extinguish a flame of the _Radiant Spark_ once it burns on a candle's wick unless the force of the wind or water causes the candle itself to topple or float away.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 170 **Usage** affixed to armor or a weapon --- A sheen of red crosses the surface of this star-shaped goldstone medallion when the light hits it. The affixed armor or weapon is warm to the touch. The spell attack roll of any spell cast by Activating this item is +7, and the spell DC is 17.
  • **Armor** You gain resistance 2 to fire.
  • **Weapon** After you cast a [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) spell by Activating the _star_, your Strikes with the weapon deal an additional 1d4 fire damage until the end of your next turn.
**Activate** Cast a Spell; **Effect** You cast [_produce flame_](/Spells.aspx?ID=236). Flaming Star **Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 170 **Price** 55 gp Flaming Star (Greater) **Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 170 **Price** 425 gp --- Resistance when affixed to armor is 5, extra damage when affixed to a weapon is 1d6, the spell attack roll is +14, and the spell DC is 24. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You cast [_fireball_](/Spells.aspx?ID=119). Flaming Star (Major) **Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 170 **Price** 1,750 gp --- Resistance when affixed to armor is 10, extra damage when affixed to a weapon is 1d8, the spell attack roll is +19, and the spell DC is 29. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You cast 4th-level [_fireball_](/Spells.aspx?ID=119). **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You cast [_wall of fire_](/Spells.aspx?ID=362).

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 170 **Usage** affixed to armor or a weapon --- A sheen of red crosses the surface of this star-shaped goldstone medallion when the light hits it. The affixed armor or weapon is warm to the touch. The spell attack roll of any spell cast by Activating this item is +7, and the spell DC is 17.
  • **Armor** You gain resistance 2 to fire.
  • **Weapon** After you cast a [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) spell by Activating the _star_, your Strikes with the weapon deal an additional 1d4 fire damage until the end of your next turn.
**Activate** Cast a Spell; **Effect** You cast [_produce flame_](/Spells.aspx?ID=236). Flaming Star **Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 170 **Price** 55 gp Flaming Star (Greater) **Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 170 **Price** 425 gp --- Resistance when affixed to armor is 5, extra damage when affixed to a weapon is 1d6, the spell attack roll is +14, and the spell DC is 24. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You cast [_fireball_](/Spells.aspx?ID=119). Flaming Star (Major) **Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 170 **Price** 1,750 gp --- Resistance when affixed to armor is 10, extra damage when affixed to a weapon is 1d8, the spell attack roll is +19, and the spell DC is 29. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You cast 4th-level [_fireball_](/Spells.aspx?ID=119). **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You cast [_wall of fire_](/Spells.aspx?ID=362).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 1+"

>
[Flare Beacon](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1112)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Gadget" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=405" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 69

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) All Pathfinder Society agents have access to all uncommon clockwork items and gadgets from Chapters 1 and 2 of this book_

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

**Access**  Due to the use of technology, all gadgets are uncommon or rare, though inventors and regions with access to inventors have access to uncommon gadgets.

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Two Actions" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Flare beacons create an incredibly bright light for a brief period of time. They are often used to signal others to the beacon's location, to coordinate assaults, to request rescue, or for other similar reasons. Higher-level beacons have a radius so large that they can be seen from miles away at night. When you Activate a flare beacon, you can either place it on the ground in a space within your reach or toss it up to 60 feet straight up. The beacon then sparks into being, casting bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light in the next 20 feet for 1 minute. A flare beacon in the air falls at a rate of 10 feet per round. Creatures adjacent to a flare beacon must succeed at a DC 15 Fortitude save or be [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) until they are no longer adjacent to it.

Additionally, on a critical failure, they are also [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1) for 1 round.

fields.text: Item 1+ Flare Beacon Uncommon Consumable Gadget Source Guns & Gears pg. 69 PFS Note All Pathfinder Society agents have access to all uncommon clockwork items and gadgets from Chapters 1 and 2 of this book Usage held in 1 hand Bulk L Access Due to the use of technology, all gadgets are uncommon or rare, though inventors and regions with access to inventors have access to uncommon gadgets. Activate Two Actions Interact Flare beacons create an incredibly bright light for a brief period of time. They are often used to signal others to the beacon’s location, to coordinate assaults, to request rescue, or for other similar reasons. Higher-level beacons have a radius so large that they can be seen from miles away at night. When you Activate a flare beacon, you can either place it on the ground in a space within your reach or toss it up to 60 feet straight up. The beacon then sparks into being, casting bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light in the next 20 feet for 1 minute. A flare beacon in the air falls at a rate of 10 feet per round. Creatures adjacent to a flare beacon must succeed at a DC 15 Fortitude save or be dazzled until they are no longer adjacent to it. Item 1 Flare Beacon (Lesser) Source Guns & Gears pg. 70 Price 4 gp Item 6 Flare Beacon (Moderate) Source Guns & Gears pg. 70 Price 35 gp The beacon shines bright light in a 60-foot radius and dim light in the next 60 feet. Creatures within a 10-foot radius of the beacon must succeed at a DC 20 Fortitude save or be dazzled until they are no longer within 10 feet of it. Item 10 Flare Beacon (Greater) Source Guns & Gears pg. 70 Price 180 gp The beacon shines bright light in a 100-foot radius and dim light in the next 100 feet. Creatures within a 20-foot radius of the beacon must succeed at a DC 27 Fortitude save or be dazzled until they are no longer within 20 feet of it. Additionally, on a critical failure, they are also blinded for 1 round. Item 16 Flare Beacon (Major) Source Guns & Gears pg. 70 Price 1,500 gp The beacon shines bright light in a 180-foot radius and dim light in the next 180 feet. Creatures within a 30-foot radius of the beacon must succeed at a DC 35 Fortitude save or be dazzled until they are no longer within 30 feet of it. Additionally, on a critical failure, they are also blinded for 1 round.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 7+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Flask Of Elements](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5243)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=564" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 104

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

While the elemental once imprisoned in this flask has long departed, some of its energy is still contained within, ready to be released when the flask is broken. You activate a _flask of elements_ by removing a wax seal from the stopper. If you or anyone else hurls the flask (another Interact action), it explodes where it lands. Your toss can place the center of the explosion—a 20-foot burst—anywhere within 60 feet, though at the GM’s discretion, you might need to make an attack roll if the throw is unusually challenging. If no one hurls the flask by the start of your next turn, it shatters harmlessly. The effect of the explosion depends on the type of flask.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
level="2"
right="Item 7"
pfs="Standard"
>
Flask Of Elemental Air
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 104

**Price** 70 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

The flask explodes in a swirl of frigid air, which has the air and [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555) traits. Creatures within the area take 4d6 cold damage with a DC 23 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save. The ground in the area is coated with ice and becomes [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366) for 1 hour.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 7"
pfs="Standard"
>
Flask Of Elemental Earth
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 104

**Price** 70 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

The flask explodes in shards of glass that grow into sharp spikes; this explosion has the earth trait. Creatures within the area take 3d6 piercing damage with a DC 23 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save. The ground in the area becomes hazardous terrain for 1 hour, and any creature that moves into one of these squares or ends its turn in one takes 1d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86). A creature can take this damage only once per turn.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 7"
pfs="Standard"
>
Flask Of Elemental Water
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 104

**Price** 70 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

The flask explodes in a thick cloud that unleashes a downpour, which has the [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=732) trait. Creatures within the area take 3d6 bludgeoning damage with a DC 23 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save. The rain extinguishes all non-magical fires in the area, and the ground becomes a [quicksand](/Hazards.aspx?ID=493) hazard as large as the area.

The ground in the area becomes hazardous terrain for 1 hour, and any creature that moves into one of these squares or ends its turn in one takes 1d6 persistent bleed damage. A creature can take this damage only once per turn. Item 7 Flask Of Elemental Water Source Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence pg. 104 Price 70 gp Bulk L The flask explodes in a thick cloud that unleashes a downpour, which has the water trait. Creatures within the area take 3d6 bludgeoning damage with a DC 23 basic Reflex save. The rain extinguishes all non-magical fires in the area, and the ground becomes a quicksand hazard as large as the area.

<traits>
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 184

**Price** 25 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This is a metal drinking flask, 4 inches in diameter and 10 inches tall. Its screw top is covered by four simple metal cups that nest together.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Make an Impression;     **Effect** If you share drinks from a _flask of fellowship_ as part of your Make an Impression action, the drink that pours from the flask happens to be exactly what the target of your efforts would most like to have a dram or two of—wine, spirits, hot ginger tea, or ice cold water with lemon, for example. You gain a +1 item bonus on your [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) check. 

The GM can disallow the flask's use if it doesn't make sense in the moment for you to pull out a flask and start pouring, if drinks are inappropriate for the occasion, or if your target is absolutely not interested in sharing a drink with you. Drinks from the _flask of fellowship_ are entirely social; they won't intoxicate anyone, nor alleviate serious thirst.
