In addition to the ability to recreate immolated documents, you can immolate a [scroll](/Rules.aspx?ID=720) containing a 1st-level spell with the [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) or [negative](/Traits.aspx?ID=118) trait that takes no more than three actions to cast. Doing so stores the scroll's magic inside of the scroll case in order to reuse it later. Only a single spell can be stored this way at a time, and immolating scrolls containing a higher-level spell simply destroys the scroll without storing the magic. When you immolate a new spell scroll in the case, the previous one is lost. Enough of the scroll's magic is lost in this process that you can't use the case to recreate the scroll for the purposes of [Learning a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=25).

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action to Three Actions" /> envision, Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** The last object burned was a scroll containing an appropriate spell; **Effect** You cast the stored spell as if you were activating the scroll.

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 48 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L **Activate**([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) --- A fury cocktail is a fortifying ginger beer spiked with rum and a mixer. It's rumored to have originated from a barbarian-themed festival in a popular mead hall specializing in alchemical beverages. **Benefit** You gain an item bonus to melee attack rolls and an additional effect depending on the additive chosen when the brew is created.
  • **Animalistic** Lemon juice and powdered claws or talons are added to the cocktail. You gain an [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attack in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) group of your choice between a jaws attack that deals 1d6 piercing damage or a claw attack that has the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170) trait and deals 1d4 slashing damage.
  • **Double** This cocktail is just stronger, with more ginger and more rum. You gain resistance 1 to physical damage. The resistance increases to 2 for a moderate fury cocktail or 5 for a greater fury cocktail.
  • **Mournful** A few flower petals add a powerful aroma to the drink. You gain resistance 1 to void damage, or resistance 1 to vitality damage if you have the [void healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=83) ability. The resistance increases to 5 for a moderate fury cocktail or 10 for a greater fury cocktail.
  • **Skeptical** A splash of bitters gives the drink a more complex flavor. You gain a +1 item bonus to saves against magic. This bonus is +2 for a moderate fury cocktail or +3 for a greater fury cocktail.
  • **Titanic** Yuzu juice and powdered giant hair are added to this cocktail. If you're Medium or smaller, you gain the following effects: you become Large, are [clumsy 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3), and increase your [reach](/Traits.aspx?ID=192) by 5 feet (or by 10 feet if you started out Tiny).
  • **Wyrmhide** Pomegranate juice and elemental reagents are added to the cocktail. You gain resistance 1 to acid, cold, electricity, fire, and poison damage. The resistance increases to 5 for a moderate fury cocktail or 10 for a greater fury cocktail.
**Drawback** You take a –1 penalty to AC and a –2 penalty to Reflex saves. Fury Cocktail (Lesser) **Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 48 **Price** 15 gp **Bulk** L --- You gain a +2 item bonus to melee attack rolls, and the duration is 10 minutes. Fury Cocktail (Moderate) **Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 48 **Price** 360 gp **Bulk** L --- You gain a +3 item bonus to melee attack rolls, and the duration is 1 hour. Fury Cocktail (Greater) **Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 48 **Price** 4,000 gp **Bulk** L --- You gain a +4 item bonus to melee attack rolls, and the duration is 1 hour.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 5"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Gadget Skates](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1113)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Clockwork" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=331" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Gadget" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=405" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 70

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) All Pathfinder Society agents have access to all uncommon clockwork items and gadgets from Chapters 1 and 2 of this book_

**Price** 21 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn (attached to footwear or feet)

**Bulk** L
</row>

**Access** Characters from Absalom, New Thassilon, Alkenstar, Dongun Hold, or especially technological regions of Arcadia like the Deadshot Lands have access to uncommon clockwork items from the first two chapters of this book. Due to the use of technology, all gadgets are uncommon or rare, though inventors and regions with access to inventors have access to uncommon gadgets.

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><row><actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=114))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Gadget skates are metal devices that come in pairs and strap onto existing footwear (or a creature's feet).

 When you Activate gadget skates, clockwork gears reveal small wheels that propel you along the ground, moving you up to twice your Speed. During this movement, you must succeed at a DC 20 [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) check to turn up to 90 degrees, and you can't turn more than once or more than 90 degrees. During the activation and after the activation is complete, you can't Stride, Step, or otherwise move on the ground until the end of your next turn. However, you can use this movement instead of a Stride to perform a [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=36) or [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=37) just after the activation ends, in the direction of your last movement using the gadget skates.

 You can Sustain the Activation of your gadget skates for up to 1 minute. Starting on the turn after you Activate the gadget skates, the first time you Sustain the Activation each turn, you gain the effects of the activation again: you move up to twice your Speed in the same direction as your last movement with the gadget skates, and the restrictions continue to apply until you choose to cease Sustaining the Activation or you reach the maximum duration. Once the effect ends, the skates fall away and you can move normally.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 191

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn eyepiece

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These wire-rim glasses appear to be [_glasses of sociability_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1057), making you think they grant a +1 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) when they grant none. The GM secretly adjusts your Diplomacy checks to ignore the bonus, and if you have multiple +1 item bonuses to Diplomacy, the glasses take precedence, negating those bonuses.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))    **Effect** Like _glasses of sociability_, with the same limitations, you stare at another creature. If you've met and exchanged names, you expect to instantly remember the target's name. However, you recall the worst possible incorrect name, such as mistaking a famous artist for their hated rival. This blunder doesn't prevent you from realizing the creature's real name after you've been corrected. Once you use this activation, the glasses fuse to you.

</column>

If you’ve met and exchanged names, you expect to instantly remember the target’s name. However, you recall the worst possible incorrect name, such as mistaking a famous artist for their hated rival. This blunder doesn’t prevent you from realizing the creature’s real name after you’ve been corrected. Once you use this activation, the glasses fuse to you.

 **Secondary Effect** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56)) **Trigger** You're hit by a melee attack or touched by a creature; **Effect** You channel electricity into the triggering creature, which must succeed at a DC 24 Fortitude save or be [stunned 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36) (or stunned 2 on a critical failure). >
[Galvanic Mortal Coil](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1135)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 82

**Price** 970 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This porous steel coil wraps around a shard of onyx, supplementing the closely guarded science of [galvaspheres](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1136) with the magic of necromancy. When embedded in a body comprised of flesh, the blood and other fluids catalyze electrical pulses within the coil, activating the necromantic energies. In living creatures, this causes a dangerous surge that can damage the heart. In corpses, however, this can create a limited window of reanimation, with access to the corpse's final memories. _Galvanic mortal coils_ are even rarer than other galvaspheres, and thought by most to be merely hypothetical.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You drive the coil into a living creature that has 0 HP while attaching the other end to yourself, in order to damage their heart and possibly siphon their life force. The galvanic mortal coil casts [_death knell_](/Spells.aspx?ID=63) on the creature (DC 27).

**Activate** <actions string="" /> (10 minutes) [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** implant the coil into a corpse. The coil casts [_talking corpse_](/Spells.aspx?ID=329) on the body.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<column gap="tiny">

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) All Pathfinder Society agents have access to all uncommon clockwork items and gadgets from Chapters 1 and 2 of this book_

**Price** 20 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

---

A galvasphere animates a corpse to motion via electricity, rather than necromancy. When you Activate the galvasphere by inserting it into an adjacent intact Medium or Small humanoid corpse, the corpse animates as a galvaheart zombie for 1 minute. The galvaheart zombie has the statistics of a [zombie shambler](/Monsters.aspx?ID=423) except that it is a [construct](/Traits.aspx?ID=35) instead of an [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160), isn't [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521), can't be harmed by [positive](/Traits.aspx?ID=128) energy, and is the same size as the corpse (Medium or Small). The zombie is your [minion](/Traits.aspx?ID=109) and performs the actions you choose when you Command it. If you don't Command it, it takes no action, twitching in place as the electricity that animates it slowly expends itself.

---

A galvasphere animates a corpse to motion via electricity, rather than necromancy. When you Activate the galvasphere by inserting it into an adjacent intact Medium or Small humanoid corpse, the corpse animates as a galvaheart zombie for 1 minute. The galvaheart zombie has the statistics of a [zombie shambler](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3249) except that it is a [construct](/Traits.aspx?ID=563) instead of an [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722), isn’t [evil](/Traits.aspx?ID=64), can’t be harmed by positive energy, and is the same size as the corpse (Medium or Small). The zombie is your [minion](/Traits.aspx?ID=653) and performs the actions you choose when you [Command](/Actions.aspx?ID=2400) it. If you don’t Command it, it takes no action, twitching in place as the electricity that animates it slowly expends itself.

</title>

</row>

</row>

---

This stone figurine of a chariot pulled by two horses was used by Tekritanin adults during strategy game competitions. Sometimes, though, mischievous adolescents snatched pieces like this one for joyriding.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You place the figurine on the ground and roll it forward. As the chariot begins to move, it rapidly expands to the size of a Large [heavy chariot](/Vehicles.aspx?ID=4) pulled by two animated stone [war horses](/Monsters.aspx?ID=268). You can board the chariot and drive it up to 80 feet in a straight line. You can move through spaces occupied by creatures of size Medium or smaller, dealing 4d8+10 bludgeoning damage to those creatures. Affected creatures must attempt a DC 28 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save; on a failure, a creature is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31). The chariot returns to its figurine form once it stops moving.

---

A nigh-infinite assortment of games exist in Golarion. Simple games, including dice, a deck of cards, or dominoes, cost 5 sp. Board games vary in cost from 1 gp for dexterity games like Bungle, 3 gp for colorful children's games like Cauldron Quest, and 5 gp for complex strategy games like Kingmaker and Abendego Raiders. Lavish game sets can cost much more than these prices, as they are made of expensive components and are intricately crafted works of art unto themselves.

These dice are weighted on one side to ensure they always land with the desired number facing up. Loaded dice grant you a +1 item bonus to [Games Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) checks to gamble with the dice. You can determine a die is loaded while handling it with a successful secret DC 20 Perception check. Determining dice are loaded without handling the dice is more difficult, especially since smart cheaters switch loaded dice in and out so they don't suspiciously roll the same number over and over. In this case, an observer must succeed at a secret Perception check against the roller's Games Lore or [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) DC to notice the switches or the patterns.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 81

**Price** 1,200 gp

<row gap="medium">
**Ammunition** any

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

---

Wiry designs mark the silvery coating on a _garrote shot_. When the activated ammunition hits a target, it transforms into a silvery garrote that wraps around one of the target's appendages, dealing 2d12 [persistent slashing damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29). On a critical hit, it wraps around the target's throat if it has one, and the target [can't breathe](/Rules.aspx?ID=468) until the persistent damage ends. If the persistent damage kills the target, the garrote severs the appendage it's wrapped around.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Air" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=5" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 149

**Price** 85 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn mask

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This black canvas mask covers your mouth and nose, with thick tubes coming from the sides. While wearing this mask, you gain a +1 item bonus to saves against [inhaled](/Traits.aspx?ID=634) [poisons](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), inhaled diseases, and [olfactory](/Traits.aspx?ID=664) effects.

**Activate—Breathe Clean** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Your mask springs to life, pumping clean air into your nose and mouth. For 1 round, you are [immune](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) to inhaled poisons, inhaled diseases, and olfactory effects. If you have ongoing effects due to such an effect from before activating the mask, those effects continue as normal. If the air around you is unbreathable, you are underwater, or you are in a vacuum, you can breathe normally.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 3+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Gate Attenuator](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2654)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 224

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_Gate attenuators_ are typically worn near the body's core and are  shaped like portals or passageways, making literal the elemental gates [kineticists](/Classes.aspx?ID=23) possess within their bodies. The appearance can vary from a simple disk with a hole in the middle to a design matching a city gate of a particular settlement. If you're a kineticist, the attenuator grants you a +1 item bonus to your impulse attack modifier (but not to your impulse DC). When you invest a _gate attenuator_, attune it to one element of your choice. Designs on the attenuator's surface transform to match that element, and the attenuator gains the element's trait until it's no longer invested or is attuned to a different element.

**Activate—Elemental Spell** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The _gate attenuator_ casts a 1st-rank spell, with a spell attack modifier of +7 and spell DC of 17. If you're a kineticist and the spell's element matches one of your kinetic elements, you can use your impulse attack modifier instead of the spell attack modifier or your impulse DC instead of the spell DC. The spell corresponds to the element the item is attuned to, and it gains that element's trait if it doesn't already have it: **air** [_gust of wind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=143), **earth** [_pummeling rubble_](/Spells.aspx?ID=708), **fire** [_dehydrate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1351), **metal** [_thunderstrike_](/Spells.aspx?ID=283), **water** [_snowball_](/Spells.aspx?ID=540), or **wood** [_flourishing flora_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1401).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
Gate Attenuator
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 224

**Price** 60 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

pfs="Standard"
>
Gate Attenuator (Greater)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 224

**Price** 1,400 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

The item bonus to your impulse attack modifier is +2. The activation casts a 5th-rank spell, with a spell attack modifier of +18 and a spell DC of 28: **air** [_pressure zone_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1318), **earth** [_sand form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1340), **fire** [_flames of ego_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1357), **metal** [_impaling spike_](/Spells.aspx?ID=697), **water** [_freezing rain_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1388), or **wood** [_entwined roots_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1400).

<title
level="2"
right="Item 17"
pfs="Standard"
>
Gate Attenuator (Major)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Apex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=532" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 224

**Price** 15,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

A _major gate attenuator_ has the [apex](/Traits.aspx?ID=10) trait. When you invest it, you either increase your Constitution modifier by 1 or increase it to +4, whichever would give you a higher score. The item bonus to your impulse attack modifier is +2. The activation casts an 8th-rank spell, with a spell attack modifier of +27 and a spell DC of 37: **air** [_whirlwind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1033), **earth** [_earthquake_](/Spells.aspx?ID=95), **fire** [_boil blood_](/Spells.aspx?ID=874), **metal** [_rust cloud_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1377) (8th rank), **water** [_whirlpool_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1398), or **wood** [_pollen pods_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1407) (8th rank).

_Gate attenuators_ are typically worn near the body's core and are  shaped like portals or passageways, making literal the elemental gates [kineticists](/Classes.aspx?ID=23) possess within their bodies. The appearance can vary from a simple disk with a hole in the middle to a design matching a city gate of a particular settlement. If you're a kineticist, the attenuator grants you a +1 item bonus to your impulse attack modifier (but not to your impulse DC). When you invest a _gate attenuator_, attune it to one element of your choice. Designs on the attenuator's surface transform to match that element, and the attenuator gains the element's trait until it's no longer invested or is attuned to a different element.

**Activate—Elemental Spell** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The _gate attenuator_ casts a 1st-rank spell, with a spell attack modifier of +7 and spell DC of 17. If you're a kineticist and the spell's element matches one of your kinetic elements, you can use your impulse attack modifier instead of the spell attack modifier or your impulse DC instead of the spell DC. The spell corresponds to the element the item is attuned to, and it gains that element's trait if it doesn't already have it: **air** [_gust of wind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=143), **earth** [_pummeling rubble_](/Spells.aspx?ID=708), **fire** [_dehydrate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1351), **metal** [_thunderstrike_](/Spells.aspx?ID=283), **water** [_snowball_](/Spells.aspx?ID=540), or **wood** [_flourishing flora_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1401).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 20"
    pfs=""
>
[Gauntlight](/Equipment.aspx?ID=915)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Abomination Vaults</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #163: Ruins of Gauntlight](/Sources.aspx?ID=71) pg. 77

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_Gauntlight_ is much more than a 115-foot-tall lighthouse rising from the heart of an old ruin in Fogfen—its pale stone walls extend far below the ruins, passing through eight different dungeon levels and finally terminating at the ninth level below the surface, where its deep foundation centers on an ominous chamber where, long ago, [Nhimbaloth](/Deities.aspx?ID=163) herself once physically brushed against this world. Once she finished its physical construction, the sorcerer Belcorra Haruvex used this spot as a source of power to infuse the walls, floors, and ceilings of each of _Gauntlight's_ levels with eldritch power. The lens at the apex of the lighthouse would have, in time, been able to focus this lingering eldritch energy into a powerful beam, but Belcorra's plans were cut short before she could replace the mundane lenses with dangerous magical ones.

 As an artifact, _Gauntlight_ can't be damaged by normal means. Its walls are impenetrable and impervious to any attempt to breach them by anybody except for followers of Nhimbaloth. They block effects that allow temporary passage, such as [_passwall_](/Spells.aspx?ID=216), and also create a barrier against dimensional travel. The walls attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=156) effects and planar travel into or out of areas within _Gauntlight_ and efforts to summon creatures into the area (using a +37 counteract modifier); this effect does not stop a summoned creature from departing when the summoning ends.

 In _Gauntlight's_ current state of diminished functionality, it can be activated only in the two ways below. By swapping in a series of magical lighthouse lenses that focus Nhimbaloth's baleful gaze—lenses so powerful that even Belcorra takes special care with them—the artifact gains significantly greater power, including the ability to reach all the way to Absalom and to activate its effects every minute. These lenses are described in “Eyes of Empty Death,” the third adventure in the Abomination Vaults Adventure Path.

 To activate _Gauntlight_, a creature must be in the deepest portion of the artifact (this chamber is in the Temple level and is presented in “Eyes of Empty Death”). From this point, a creature can observe the world outside remotely through _Gauntlight's_ lens, including any area _Gauntlight's_ beam can reach.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per month;   **Effect** A pale blue beam shines from _Gauntlight's_ lens and illuminates a 30-foot-radius burst centered on any point within 1 mile. The light saturates the region, causing any corpses in the area or within 10 feet of the surface of the illuminated area to animate as level –1 undead (typically as [skeleton guards](/Monsters.aspx?ID=372) or [zombie shamblers](/Monsters.aspx?ID=423)). Once animated, the undead remain active until slain. Until then, they remain uncontrolled and are driven only by the desire to slaughter the living. If _Gauntlight_ is fully restored, the undead instead animate as any Common [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) of 15th level or less, as the user wishes.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per month;   **Effect** A pale blue beam shines from _Gauntlight's_ lens and illuminates a 30-foot-radius burst centered on any point within 1 mile. The user chooses one creature of 4th level or less that is physically located within _Gauntlight_; this creature is then is teleported to any point within this illumination radius. If _Gauntlight_ is fully restored, any number of creatures within _Gauntlight_ of 15th level or lower can be transported. This is a [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=156) effect.

**Destruction** If Belcorra's ghost is permanently destroyed, _Gauntlight_ loses all of its magical properties and collapses in on itself all the way down to its base, leaving an incredibly deep pit in the Fogfen.

fields.text: Item 20 Gauntlight May contain spoilers from Abomination Vaults Unique Artifact Magical Necromancy Source Pathfinder #163: Ruins of Gauntlight pg. 77 Gauntlight is much more than a 115-foot-tall lighthouse rising from the heart of an old ruin in Fogfen—its pale stone walls extend far below the ruins, passing through eight different dungeon levels and finally terminating at the ninth level below the surface, where its deep foundation centers on an ominous chamber where, long ago, Nhimbaloth herself once physically brushed against this world. Once she finished its physical construction, the sorcerer Belcorra Haruvex used this spot as a source of power to infuse the walls, floors, and ceilings of each of Gauntlight's levels with eldritch power. The lens at the apex of the lighthouse would have, in time, been able to focus this lingering eldritch energy into a powerful beam, but Belcorra's plans were cut short before she could replace the mundane lenses with dangerous magical ones. As an artifact, Gauntlight can't be damaged by normal means. Its walls are impenetrable and impervious to any attempt to breach them by anybody except for followers of Nhimbaloth. They block effects that allow temporary passage, such as passwall , and also create a barrier against dimensional travel. The walls attempt to counteract teleportation effects and planar travel into or out of areas within Gauntlight and efforts to summon creatures into the area (using a +37 counteract modifier); this effect does not stop a summoned creature from departing when the summoning ends. In Gauntlight's current state of diminished functionality, it can be activated only in the two ways below. By swapping in a series of magical lighthouse lenses that focus Nhimbaloth's baleful gaze—lenses so powerful that even Belcorra takes special care with them—the artifact gains significantly greater power, including the ability to reach all the way to Absalom and to activate its effects every minute. These lenses are described in “Eyes of Empty Death,” the third adventure in the Abomination Vaults Adventure Path. To activate Gauntlight , a creature must be in the deepest portion of the artifact (this chamber is in the Temple level and is presented in “Eyes of Empty Death”). From this point, a creature can observe the world outside remotely through Gauntlight's lens, including any area Gauntlight's beam can reach. Activate Three Actions Interact; Frequency once per month; Effect A pale blue beam shines from Gauntlight's lens and illuminates a 30-foot-radius burst centered on any point within 1 mile. The light saturates the region, causing any corpses in the area or within 10 feet of the surface of the illuminated area to animate as level –1 undead (typically as skeleton guards or zombie shamblers). Once animated, the undead remain active until slain. Until then, they remain uncontrolled and are driven only by the desire to slaughter the living. If Gauntlight is fully restored, the undead instead animate as any Common undead of 15th level or less, as the user wishes. Activate Three Actions Interact; Frequency once per month; Effect A pale blue beam shines from Gauntlight's lens and illuminates a 30-foot-radius burst centered on any point within 1 mile. The user chooses one creature of 4th level or less that is physically located within Gauntlight ; this creature is then is teleported to any point within this illumination radius. If Gauntlight is fully restored, any number of creatures within Gauntlight of 15th level or lower can be transported. This is a teleportation effect. Destruction If Belcorra's ghost is permanently destroyed, Gauntlight loses all of its magical properties and collapses in on itself all the way down to its base, leaving an incredibly deep pit in the Fogfen.

<traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [High Seas](/Sources.aspx?ID=351) pg. 64

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Seeing all Red Mantis contracts is outside the scope of PFS play._

**Price** 1,400 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn eyepiece

**Bulk** L
</row>

**Access** You're a member of the Red Mantis Assassins

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These glasses have faceted red lenses like those of a mantis and are popular as a less ostentatious alternative to a full mask. While wearing the _gaze of the mantis_, your field of view increases to give you better awareness of your surroundings. You gain a +2 item bonus to visual Perception checks and cannot be [flanked](/Rules.aspx?ID=2375). 

**Activate—Target Sense** <actions string="Single Action" /> ;  **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** You’re a Red Mantis assassin; **Effect** You learn the distance to and direction of all creatures that have a Red Mantis contract on them within 10 miles. If one of these creatures is within 100 feet, you also know any afflictions, conditions, and spells affecting them. This awareness lasts for 1 hour.

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 54 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L **Activate**([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) --- Gearbinder oil comes in a sealed pump that can squirt the oil a short distance. The oil is designed to flow through complex mechanisms and, agitated through mechanical action, foam up and form a paste that binds the works. The oil is effective against articulated constructs and machinery, including many [constructs](/Traits.aspx?ID=35), [clockworks](/Traits.aspx?ID=331), and [mechanical](/Traits.aspx?ID=105) hazards. You apply the oil to the target you want to bind, which must be within 10 feet of you. After the oil is applied, at the end of any round during which the target took an action with the [attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=15), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104), or [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=114) trait, it must attempt a Fortitude save against a DC determined by the oil's type. A mechanism that's [slowed 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) or more by gearbinder oil also can't use reactions. Gearbinder oil functions for up to 6 rounds before becoming an inert, oily residue. **Critical Success** The oil becomes inert, and the effect ends.
**Success** The target reduces its slowed condition by 1. If the slowed condition's value is 0, the effect ends.
**Failure** The target increases its slowed condition by 1, to a maximum of slowed 3.
**Critical Failure** The target increases its slowed condition by 2, to a maximum of slowed 3.     level="1"
    right="Item 17"
    pfs=""
>
[Gearblade](/Equipment.aspx?ID=896)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Agents of Edgewatch</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Clockwork" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=331" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #161: Belly of the Black Whale](/Sources.aspx?ID=51) pg. 79

**Price** 13,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 or 2 hands

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Bastard Sword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=15), [Greatsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=24), [Longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=31), [Shortsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=43), [Greatclub](/Weapons.aspx?ID=22)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Shaped like a blade made from spinning gears, this _+2 [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) weapon_ can catch enemy weapons and grind up foes. In order to function, the _gearblade_ must be wound for 10 minutes once every 24 hours. During this process, you can reconfigure the weapon to transform into a [bastard sword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=15), [greatsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=24), [longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=31), or [shortsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=43). It then gains all the features of the chosen weapon except that its Bulk is always 2 and it gains the [disarm](/Traits.aspx?ID=175) weapon trait and the [versatile B](/Traits.aspx?ID=200) weapon trait (which replaces any other versatile trait the weapon might have). If you don't wind the _gearblade_, it becomes inert and has the statistics of a [greatclub](/Weapons.aspx?ID=22).

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You roll a critical success to [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=41) a target with the _gearblade_; **Requirements** You've wound the _gearblade_ for 10 minutes within the last 24 hours; **Effect** The target's weapon is pulled through the _gearblade's_ gears and shoots out the other side, landing 20 feet away in a direction of your choice. The target must attempt a DC 36 Reflex save. On a failure, the limb holding their weapon is also pulled into the _gearblade_, and the creature takes 3d12 bludgeoning damage. On a critical failure, they take 6d12 bludgeoning damage and the limb becomes unusable until healed by a [_regenerate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=248) spell or a similar effect.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

Gecko pads are thin, clockwork devices shaped like palms, which can be strapped onto existing handwear or a creature's hands. When activated, they whir to life and improve your grip on surfaces, while slowly releasing a sticky substance stored within the device's surface to help you climb. The pads give you a climb Speed equal to your Speed as long as your hands are free.

---

_Note from Nethys: This item is a constituent part of the [Gelid Shard](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=201) archetype using the [archetype artifact](/Rules.aspx?ID=1961) rules._

This crystal shard shimmers with its own light even as it seems to draw the heat out of its surroundings. Plunging it into your heart grants you the tranquil lethality of deepest winter, but the more you draw upon its power, the colder your heart grows. Your frozen heart dulls your emotions. When you gain a bonus from an [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60) effect, that bonus is reduced by 1, to a minimum of 0. At 10th level, the bonus is reduced by 2. Your dulled emotions make it hard to relate to others; the DC of checks to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50) or [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=51) a favor of other creatures, or to [Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=75) in such attempts, is increased by +2. You gain resistance to cold equal to your level and a +2 status bonus to all saves against emotion effects.

**Destruction** The _gelid shard_ must be left exposed in the [Plane of Fire](/Planes.aspx?ID=6) for a week and a day, then smashed with an [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=271) hammer by someone who felt true love for the shard's creator.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [The Mwangi Expanse](/Sources.aspx?ID=89) pg. 34

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) The genealogy mask may be purchased to strengthen your character’s story and roleplay, but cannot be used to impact gameplay during Organized Play adventures._

**Price** 10 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

**Bulk** L
</row>

**Access** Alijae ethnicity

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These large masks are forged of precious metals or carved of wood and tasked with guarding the history of a family. Most Alijae are granted a _genealogy_ mask when they come of age, which they bequeath to their next of kin upon death. When a member of the family recounted in the _genealogy mask_ performs a particularly significant event while wearing the mask, its eyes and ears animate, allowing the item to witness and record the deeds for posterity. Different families have different standards for their _genealogy masks_—some may value accuracy and objective, clinical facts, while others may relish embellishing their stories to the very brink of believability in the name of a good story.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You ask the mask about the deeds of a particular ancestor, and the mask speaks for 10 minutes, recalling the tales it knows about that ancestor. The mask is limited by what information a particular ancestor shared with it. 

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

---

A _commander’s signet_ is typically a silver ring emblazoned with the coat of arms or heraldry of a wealthy noble family, or the insignia of a mercenary group. A badge of office often worn by soldiers during the Shining Crusade in Ustalav, many _commander’s signets_ bear iconography associated with Aroden, Arazni, or Iomedae, but those found in this adventure bear the heraldry of the Arudora family. The signet grants an item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks made to Make an Impression or to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) checks made to Coerce, and can be activated to bolster the morale of a nearby target. 

**Activate—Bolster Bravery** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You fill a creature you touch with bravery and heroic conviction, granting it a status bonus to attack rolls, Perception checks, saving throws, and skill checks for 1 minute. The status bonus is doubled for saving throws made against fear effects.

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Perception** +22; precise vision 30 feet, imprecise hearing 30 feet, constant [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=66)

**Communication** speech ([Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2), and eight other common languages)

**Skills** [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) +34, seven [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) skills +28, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) +28, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +28

**Int** +8, **Wis** +0, **Cha** +4

</column>

---        

The _genius diadem_ is a _crown of intellect_ that typically acts like an arrogant professor or mentor, often boasting that it is a certified greater intellect and far superior to your own intelligence, even after the benefits the diadem grants you. The _genius diadem_ encourages you to learn things for yourself rather than actually attempting to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) for you, though you or your allies might be able to play on its arrogance using [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) to trick it into doing so. In addition to allowing you to activate it, the diadem can use the Search Your Mind activation with its own actions, though if it does so, the diadem gains the benefits instead of you. Only the diadem can use the following activation.

**Activate—Brain Drain** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** The _genius diadem_ casts 7th-rank [_never mind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1614).

A _ghast stiletto_ is a _[+1](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2830) [dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=358)_ wrapped in the still-undead skin of a [ghast](/Monsters.aspx?ID=219). While you wield the dagger, you gain a +1 status bonus to all saves against [paralysis](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85).

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command, Interact ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117), [olfactory](/Traits.aspx?ID=664)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** The _ghast stiletto_ afflicts the next living target struck by the dagger with a terrible wound that emits the foul stench of the grave. For the next minute, the target creature, as well as any creatures within a 10-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387), must succeed at a DC 16 Fortitude save or become [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) 1 (plus [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 as long as it’s sickened on a critical failure). While within the emanation, the creature takes a –2 circumstance penalty to saves against [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578) and to recover from the sickened condition. A creature that succeeds at its save is temporarily immune for 1 minute.

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include skin from a [ghast](/Monsters.aspx?ID=219).

This black cooking pot can produce a feast fit for [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160).

_Ghost ammunition_ is cool to the touch. These spring-loaded metal canisters contain a mixture of chemicals and salts that drain and disintegrate nearby undead creatures. A ghost charge deals the listed vitality damage and splash damage, though as usual for [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509) damage, this damage harms only undead and creatures with [void healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=83). Ghost charges are designed to explode even on contact with a spiritual substance, making them ideal for damaging [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=632) undead. A primary target that takes damage from a ghost charge becomes [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) until the start of your next turn. Many types grant an item bonus to attack rolls.

These spring-loaded metal canisters contain a mixture of chemicals and salts that drain and disintegrate nearby [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) creatures. A ghost charge deals the listed positive damage and splash damage, though as usual for positive damage, this damage harms only undead and creatures with [negative healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=42). Ghost charges are designed to explode even on contact with a spiritual substance, making them ideal for damaging [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) undead. A primary target that takes damage from a ghost charge becomes [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13) until the start of your next turn. Many types grant an item bonus to attack rolls.

These spring-loaded metal canisters contain a mixture of chemicals and salts that drain and disintegrate nearby undead creatures. A ghost charge deals the listed vitality damage and splash damage, though as usual for [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509) damage, this damage harms only undead and creatures with [void healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=83). Ghost charges are designed to explode even on contact with a spiritual substance, making them ideal for damaging [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=632) undead. A primary target that takes damage from a ghost charge becomes [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) until the start of your next turn. Many types grant an item bonus to attack rolls.

>
[Ghost Courier Fulu](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2034)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Fulu" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=378" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 77

**Price** 100 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Two Actions" /><row>([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The inscription on a _ghost courier fulu_ leaves space for a message, and a prominent red stamp indicates which [_ghost delivery fulu_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2035) this fulu homes in on (see below). When you Activate this fulu, you dictate a message up to 25 words long that then magically appears on the paper in the language you spoke. The fulu then disappears into the [Ethereal Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=34), arriving at the assigned ghost delivery fulu in 2d10 hours, provided that fulu is within 500 miles. There, the fulu’s magic dissipates, but the message remains. If the fulu takes any damage in transit, it has a 50% chance to drop back into [the Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=26), intact but bereft of magic.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><row>10 minutes (Interact)</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This pale-blue ink dries rapidly, becoming fully transparent 1 minute after application. The ink glows red when exposed to heat, such as that from a [torch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=60) or other open flame. This glow lasts only as long as the ink is exposed to heat, after which the ink becomes invisible again. The crafter of the ghost ink can alter the formula slightly to instead make the ink sensitive to sunlight, starlight, magical light, or heatless light created by an alchemical effect such as a [sunrod](/Equipment.aspx?ID=137).

 While the text isn't glowing, a creature closely examining a surface marked with ghost ink can detect the presence of the ink with a successful DC 25 Perception check. On a critical success, they can make out the ink well enough to use [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) to [Decipher Writing](/Actions.aspx?ID=22). One vial of ghost ink is sufficient to write a page worth of text.

</column>

>
[Ghost Lantern](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2191)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Light" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=100" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 115

**Price** 1,850 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Crafted from [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2916), this black hooded [lantern](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2730) has gray glass and lenses that emit a pale gray light when the lantern is lit. Anything this light falls on looks gray or desaturated. The lantern uses oil as a standard hooded lantern. The lantern’s light shines within the [Ethereal Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=34) as well as [the Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=26). On any other plane, the light functions as a normal hooded lantern.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** The lantern's shutters are open; **Effect** You concentrate on the lantern’s light to soften the boundary between the [Ethereal Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=34) and [the Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=26). Any creature in the lantern’s bright light on the Universe gains the effects of the [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2840) property rune on all its weapons and unarmed attacks. If an affected weapon or attack is [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644) and already has the maximum number of property runes, the wielder can choose one to suppress to gain ghost touch. This benefit lasts for 5 minutes or until the shutters are closed, whichever comes first. It applies to a creature only while it’s in the lantern’s [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2402), and if the creature leaves the light and returns it regains the benefit once more.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

fields.text: Item 7 Ghost Scarf May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts Rare Invested Magical Source Season of Ghosts (Hardcover) pg. 307 Price 360 gp Usage worn belt or scarf This 6-foot-long scarf shimmers with the silvery light of the River of Souls while worn, providing illumination equivalent to that of a candle. You can deactivate or activate this radiance as an Interact action. The dangling lengths of a ghost scarf softly billow in the presence of haunts, granting the wearer a +1 item bonus to all Perception checks and Perception DCs to resolve discovering a haunt or rolling initiative when a haunt triggers. Activate—Ghost Slayer's Caress Single Action (concentrate) Frequency once per day; Effect The scarf extends silvery threads that wrap around a weapon you carry, granting the effects of a ghost touch property rune to that weapon for 5 minutes. If the weapon already bears a ghost touch rune, you instead gain a +1 item bonus to Fortitude saves against effects from incorporeal undead for 5 minutes.

>
[Ghost Stone](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3448)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Seven Dooms for Sandpoint</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #200: Seven Dooms for Sandpoint](/Sources.aspx?ID=229) pg. 183

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 18
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The _Ghost Stone_ is a stationary magic item, a 10-foot-long spindle-shaped crystal floating and slowly rotating within a hemispherical chamber in the Pit (area **E10**). If moved from this chamber, the _Ghost Stone_ is destroyed. It can also be destroyed via damage (AC 28, Hardness 16, HP 60). If it's destroyed, the trapped Varisian spirits within are finally released; as a vortex of vaguely humanoid shapes swirls around the room, all PCs in area **E10** are filled with sensations of elation and freedom. The departing ghosts grant each PC the first activation result below, but after that, the _Ghost Stone_ crashes to the ground and shatters into mundane crystal, forever destroyed. 

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> (command, envision, Interact);     **Effect** The _Ghost Stone_ grants a terrifying vision of doom. For the PCs, this vision is of seven apocalyptic dooms that descend upon Sandpoint.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> 10 minutes (command, envision, Interact);  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The _Ghost Stone_ casts [_read omens_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1647) to your specifications.

</column>

---

A weapon etched with this rune can harm creatures without physical form. A _ghost touch_ weapon is particularly effective against [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) creatures, which almost always have a specific vulnerability to ghost touch weapons. Incorporeal creatures can touch, hold, and wield ghost touch weapons (unlike most physical objects).

fields.text: Item 12+ Ghostcaller's Planchette Magical Necromancy Spellheart Source Treasure Vault pg. 125 Usage affixed to armor or weapon This miniature wooden planchette is engraved with symbols designed to attract spirits. When affixed, the symbols begin to glow, and the planchette turns slightly insubstantial. The spell DC of any spell cast by activating this item is 29. Armor After you cast a necromancy spell by activating the planchette, you gain resistance 5 to all physical damage (except ghost touch ) until the start of your next turn. Attacks by incorporeal creatures (such as a ghost’s ghostly hand) count as ghost touch. Weapon After you cast a necromancy spell by activating the planchette, the affixed weapon gains the effects of the ghost touch property rune until the end of your next turn. Activate Cast a Spell; Effect You cast chill touch . Item 12 Ghostcaller's Planchette Source Treasure Vault pg. 125 Price 1,750 gp Activate Cast a Spell; Frequency once per day; Effect You cast invoke spirits . Item 18 Ghostcaller's Planchette (Greater) Source Treasure Vault pg. 125 Price 21,000 gp The resistance when affixed to armor is 10. When the planchette is affixed to a weapon, casting a necromancy spell by activating the planchette grants the weapon the effects of both the ghost touch and greater disrupting property runes. The spell DC is 38. Activate Cast a Spell; Frequency once per day; Effect You cast 7th-level invoke spirits . Activate Cast a Spell; Frequency once per day; Effect You cast tempest of shades .

A _ghostcracker_ pops and smokes when consumed. When you throw the _ghostcracker_ down in your space as part of casting an [_illusory creature_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1567) spell, the appearance of the creature twists nightmarishly. When an enemy’s attack or spell ends the _illusory creature_ spell, the creature “dies” in a disturbing fashion, rendering the enemy [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 1. From this effect, the _ghostcracker_ adds the [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), and [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) traits to the spell.

>
[Ghosthand's Comet](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2363)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 179

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The barrel of this long rifle is translucent in places, forming a swirled pattern along the metal, and its stock is formed of crimson wood. _Ghosthand's Comet_ is a _+4 [major striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [beast-bane](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1041) [greater impactful](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1062) advanced firearm_ with a [range increment](/Traits.aspx?ID=248) of 300 feet. It deals 5d8 force damage and has the [backstabber](/Traits.aspx?ID=172), [concussive](/Traits.aspx?ID=401), [kickback](/Traits.aspx?ID=409), and [fatal d12 traits](/Traits.aspx?ID=178). As a star gun, _Ghosthand's Comet_ runs on magic and doesn't use ammunition or black powder. The weapon is silent when fired.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))  **Trigger** You attempt a ranged Strike with _Ghosthand's Comet_;  **Effect** For the triggering Strike, _Ghosthand's Comet_ changes its damage type to your choice of acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))    **Effect** On your next attempt at a ranged Strike with _Ghosthand's Comet_, the shot phases through any material or magical obstacle, such as a [_wall of force_](/Spells.aspx?ID=363), in its path, ignoring all [cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=459). You must attempt the Strike by the end of your turn or this effect is lost.

**Destruction** If the [Grim Reaper](/Monsters.aspx?ID=250) slays the wielder of _Ghosthand's Comet_, the Reaper's scythe, as it strikes the killing blow, is destined to slice the star gun in half.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Illusion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=92" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Talisman" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=155" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 184

**Price** 300 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** affixed to a ranged weapon

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Free Action" /><row>([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))</row></row>

 

**Trigger** You attempt a ranged Strike with the affixed weapon while [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39).

 
</row>

</column>

---

This long strip of linen is tightly wound around the barrel of the affixed firearm or the grip of a bow. When activated, the talisman's magic dampens the sound of the triggering shot, rendering it completely silent, and additionally skews the angle of the shot, so it appears to come from a different location and direction than your actual position. You don't become automatically observed to any creatures due to making the triggering Strike.

</title>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

---

A _ghoul stiletto_ is a _[+1](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2830) [dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=358)_ wrapped in the still-undead skin of a [ghoul](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=419). While you wield the dagger, you gain a +1 status bonus to all saves against [curses](/Traits.aspx?ID=566) and [olfactory](/Traits.aspx?ID=664) effects.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [olfactory](/Traits.aspx?ID=664)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** The _ghoul stiletto_ afflicts the next living target struck by the dagger with a terrible wound that emits the foul stench of the grave. The creature emits a stench [aura](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=53) in a 10-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) for 1 minute. During that time, the affected creature, as well as any creature that starts or ends its turn in the aura, must succeed at a DC 17 Fortitude save or become [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) 1 (plus [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 as long as it’s sickened on a critical failure). A creature that succeeds at its save is temporarily immune to all stench auras for 1 minute.

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include skin from a [ghoul](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=419).

This sturdy pole has a rope attached to one end in a loop with the other end extending to the handle. You can pull the handle side of the rope to tighten the loop. Using this loop, you can [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376) without having a free hand. A creature grappled this way receives a –2 circumstance penalty to attack rolls when [Striking](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with an unarmed attack. Due to limitations in the size of the loop, a catch pole can only be used on creatures sized Medium or smaller.

Three dried tentacles from a giant squid studded with pufferfish spines have been twisted together to form this robust _[+1](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2830) [wounding](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2854) [whip](/Weapons.aspx?ID=404)_. With a clever flick of the wrist, they can be unfurled into a deadly arc of poisonous barbs.

**Activate—Poison Barrage** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You lash out with the whip’s three tentacles in a 15-foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386). Each creature inside the cone must attempt a DC 27 basic Fortitude save or take 4d6 poison damage. On a critical failure, the creature also takes 1d6 [persistent poison damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86).

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include three tentacles from a [giant squid](/Monsters.aspx?ID=820).

Activate—Poison Barrage Two Actions (manipulate) Frequency once per hour; Effect You lash out with the whip’s three tentacles in a 15-foot cone. Craft Requirements The initial raw materials must include three tentacles from a giant squid.

>
[Gift of Olives](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3991)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Myth-Speaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Plant" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=668" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #216: The Acropolis Pyre](/Sources.aspx?ID=271) pg. 81

**Price** 48 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This expertly trimmed olive branch remains lush and vibrant, even months after being ritually harvested. With a little soil and patience, it can quickly grow into a sheltering tree that later bestows the user with a new gift of olives.

**Activate—Sew the Cutting** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623), [manipulate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2229), [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=668))   **Requirements** You are outside and standing atop an unoccupied 5-foot square with some soil; **Effect** You drive one end of the cutting into the soil. The cutting immediately grows into an olive tree whose boughs shelter a 15-foot-diameter area. Creatures in the sheltered area gain resistance 3 to any [environmental damage](/Rules.aspx?ID=2769), gain a +1 status bonus to saving throws against [environmental](/Traits.aspx?ID=591) hazards, and gain a +1 status bonus to [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) checks to [Subsist](/Actions.aspx?ID=2368). After 10 minutes, the tree sprouts 8 olives, each of which can be eaten as an action to restore 1 Hit Point and nourish the eater as if they had consumed a full meal. After 8 hours, the olives lose their potency, and the _gift of olives_ cutting detaches from the tree and falls harmlessly to the ground. The olive tree loses its protective abilities and becomes a normal, non-magical olive tree that survives so long as it's growing in a suitable location.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 16"
    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Gift of the Poisoned Heart](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1642)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Evil" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=64" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 160

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="" /><row>1 minute (command, Interact)</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Those who fail to see the curse view this object as a priceless gift, capable of restoring life to the deceased, but deep in the heart of this diamond lies a single flaw: a fissured occlusion of sickly, tainted red. To activate the diamond, place it on the relatively intact body of a creature that died within the past year. The stone shatters, restoring the recipient to life with the effects of a successful [_resurrect_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=20) ritual, except there is no limit to the level of the creature that may be revived.

 This gift of life comes with a terrible cost: the recipient believes you—and anyone else who aided in the resurrection— deliberately caused their death and revived them only in furtherance of some nefarious scheme. Having a proxy activate the _gift of the poisoned heart_ is of no use, as the item's magic sniffs out all coconspirators and uses your attempt to avoid the drawback to feed the resurrected creature's paranoia.

 No amount of information or persuasion can alleviate this mistrust, as the cursed creature twists the facts endlessly to fit their delusion. Only magic such as [_remove curse_](/Spells.aspx?ID=250) can neutralize this effect, and the subject resists any attempt to alter their beliefs by magic.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Gingerbread House](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1708)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Blood Lords</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Structure" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=153" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #182: Graveclaw](/Sources.aspx?ID=143) pg. 75

**Price** 240 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L when not activated
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A gingerbread house is made of magical gingerbread sweetened with honey and spices, and further decorated with candies and icing. Its roof tiles are made of sugar. It can be held safely in one hand but is very delicate; it's often stored within a wooden box of 1 Bulk.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> 1 minute (command, envision, Interact);     **Effect** The gingerbread house expands into a spacious and comfortable two-story cottage with a fenced yard. Although fully furnished with beds, chairs, tables, and so on, it and all its contents are made of magical gingerbread and candy. It includes a hearth that keeps the entire house warm but doesn't damage its composition. The house's cupboards are supplied with candy and cocoa sufficient to sustain 10 Medium creatures that eat roughly as much as a human for as long as the house remains activated. Creatures who spend an entire day and night resting in a _gingerbread house_ recover Hit Points at twice the normal rate; if they successfully save against an affliction, they reduce the stage of that affliction by an additional step.

 When not activated the gingerbread house has Hardness 0, 2 Hit Points, and a BT of 1. Once activated, it has Hardness 0, 40 HP, and a BT of 20. Any damage done to the activated house—including eating any part of its structure—remains when the house returns to its un-activated size.

**Craft Requirements** You can attempt [Cooking Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) checks instead of [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) checks to [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=43) a gingerbread house.

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Gods & Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=17) pg. 122

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">

<row gap="medium">

</column>

---

This _+2 [holy](/Equipment.aspx?ID=299) greater striking [glaive](/Weapons.aspx?ID=20)_ has a long, multi-tailed rainbow-colored banner affixed to the butt of the pole in the style of [Shelyn’s](/Deities.aspx?ID=17) religious symbol. While wielding the glaive, you gain a +2 item bonus on [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) and [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per round;   **Effect** You furl one of the colored tails around the pole, causing the glaive to gain the effects of your choice of the [_corrosive_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=292), [_flaming_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=295), [_frost_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=296), [_shocking_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=303), or [_thundering_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=306) property runes for 1 round, depending on the tail you chose.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You thrust the blade of the glaive into the ground, activating the power of the banner. (The blade can penetrate any non-metallic surface when used in this way, and does not leave a mark when withdrawn.) As long as the glaive is thrust into the ground and standing upright, all allies within 60 feet who can see the glaive’s banner gain a +2 item bonus to Performance checks.

</column>

On a successful Feint, the target is dazzled for 1 round.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 115

**Price** 5 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

<row gap="medium">

---

This small rod has a tiny, sharp cutting wheel made of steel on one end and a thick bulb on the other. You can use the glass cutter's wheel to score ordinary glass and use the bulb to break the piece along your scoring. It typically takes 1 minute of work to cut a hole large enough to fit your hand. If you are attempting to break the glass quietly, you must attempt a [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) check against the Perception DC of nearby creatures to go unnoticed.

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 185

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn eyepiece

**Bulk** L
</row>

</row>

---

These wire-rim glasses with large, circular lenses were invented for the sole purpose of avoiding awkward confrontations at social gatherings. They grant you a +1 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6).

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;     **Effect** You stare at another creature and instantly remember their name if you've met and exchanged names. The glasses rely on your latent memories, so if the creature is disguising their identity, the glasses don't penetrate the disguise. If a [doppelganger](/Monsters.aspx?ID=126) was disguised as an innkeeper you met, the glasses would give you the innkeeper's name, and if a noble you met before was in disguise as a masked vigilante, the glasses wouldn't reveal their name.

>
[Gleaming Cuirass](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5248)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 176

**Price** 2,500 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** 4
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Full Plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=50)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Forged with a rare silver alloy, this _[+2 resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2804) [standard-grade silver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2920) [full plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=50)_ bears protective inscriptions that strengthen the wearer's resolve and draw the attention of enemies. While wearing the armor, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590) or [possession](/Traits.aspx?ID=671) effects. 

**Activate—Face Me** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You challenge an enemy, attracting its wrath. Choose an enemy within 30 feet that can see you; it must attempt a DC 31 Will saving throw.

<column gap="tiny">

**Critical Success** The target is unaffected.

**Success** The target takes 3d8 mental damage and takes a –1 status penalty to attack rolls against creatures other than you until the end of its next turn.

**Failure** As success, but the target takes 6d8 mental damage, and the penalty lasts for 1 minute.

**Critical Failure** As success, but the target takes 12d8 mental damage, and the penalty lasts for 1 minute. In addition, the target is [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 1 and can't reduce its frightened value below 1 for the duration of the penalty.

</column>

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

[Gliding](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1831)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 12

**Price** 450 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** etched onto armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">

---

The armor allows you to make a controlled descent.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))    **Effect** You glide slowly toward the ground, 5 feet down and up to 25 feet forward through the air. Provided you spend at least 1 action gliding on your turn and haven't yet reached the ground, you remain in the air at the end of your turn. Otherwise, you fall.
